docs.title: ✅ Getting an Account Summary
docs.text:
Request: full account summary (AccountSummaryData) from MT5. Fetch all core account metrics in a single call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#account_summary (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: AccountSummary (defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: AccountSummary(AccountSummaryRequest) → AccountSummaryReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::AccountHelper::Stub#account_summary(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A single RPC returning full account state: balance, equity, credit, currency, leverage, trade mode, margin / free margin / margin level / margin mode, and server time.
  • Why you need it. Fast dashboard / CLI status; double-check login / currency / leverage; connection heartbeat via server_time.
  • Sanity check. If account_login, account_currency, account_leverage, account_equity are set → the connection is alive.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it to display real-time account state and sanity-check connectivity:

  • Dashboard / CLI status in one call.
  • Verify balance & equity before trading.
  • Terminal heartbeat via server_time / server_time_utc and server_utc_offset_seconds.

Prefer plain values? MT5Service#account_info returns a friendly Account Struct (named fields, times as numbers) instead of protobuf.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt5"

class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # Retrieves full account information in a single call.
  # Returns the raw AccountSummaryData (read fields with snake_case accessors);
  # raises ApiError on failure.
  def account_summary -> Mt5TermApi::AccountSummaryData
end

Request message:

AccountSummaryRequest {} (empty message — the SDK builds it for you; account_summary takes no arguments)

Reply message:

AccountSummaryReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountSummaryData data = 1;
    Error error = 2;
  }
}

MT5Account unwraps the oneof: it returns data on success and raises ApiError (carrying the server-side Error) otherwise.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
No parameters. account_summary takes no arguments — the SDK sends an empty AccountSummaryRequest.

There is no per-call timeout argument. Each call runs on the account's deadline (timeout, default 60 s). Tune it on the account:

acct.timeout = 15   # seconds — deadline for ordinary read RPCs

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountSummaryData
docs.text:
Field (proto) Ruby accessor Type Description account_login account_login Integer Trading account login (ID). account_balance account_balance Float Balance excluding floating P/L. account_equity account_equity Float Equity = balance + floating P/L. account_user_name account_user_name String Account holder name. account_leverage account_leverage Integer Leverage (e.g. 100 for 1:100). account_trade_mode account_trade_mode Symbol Demo / Contest / Real — see enum below. account_company_name account_company_name String Broker / company display name. account_currency account_currency String Deposit currency (e.g. "USD"). server_time server_time Timestamp Server time at response (broker time zone). .seconds → unix seconds. server_time_utc server_time_utc Timestamp The same moment in UTC. utc_timezone_server_time_shift_minutes utc_timezone_server_time_shift_minutes Integer Server offset from UTC (minutes). account_credit account_credit Float Credit amount. server_utc_offset_seconds server_utc_offset_seconds Integer Broker offset from UTC in seconds (positive = ahead). account_margin account_margin Float Margin currently used by open positions. account_margin_free account_margin_free Float Free margin available for new positions. account_margin_level account_margin_level Float Margin level in percent (equity / margin × 100); 0 when no margin is used. account_margin_mode account_margin_mode Symbol Margin mode (MT5 demo = RETAIL_HEDGING) — see enum below. account_trade_allowed account_trade_allowed Boolean Trading allowed for this account. account_trade_expert account_trade_expert Boolean Automated (EA) trading allowed. terminal_connected terminal_connected Boolean Terminal is connected to the broker. terminal_trade_allowed terminal_trade_allowed Boolean Trading is allowed in the terminal.

🧮 Floating profit: the summary has no dedicated profit field — compute account_equity - account_balance, or read account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_PROFIT).

docs.text: 💡 Enum usage note: generated protobuf enums come back as Ruby symbols. Compare against the full constant, e.g. s.account_trade_mode == :MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO.

docs.title: MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode
docs.text:
enum MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode {
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO    = 0;  // demo / practice
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST = 1;  // contest
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL    = 2;  // real trading
}

def trade_mode_to_s(mode)
  case mode
  when :MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO    then "DEMO"
  when :MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_CONTEST then "CONTEST"
  when :MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL    then "REAL"
  else "UNKNOWN(#{mode})"
  end
end

docs.title: MrpcEnumAccountMarginMode
docs.text:
enum MrpcEnumAccountMarginMode {
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_NETTING = 0;  // netting (one position per symbol)
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_EXCHANGE       = 1;  // exchange margin
  MRPC_ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING = 2;  // hedging (many positions per symbol) — typical MT5
}

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: a server-side rejection raises MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError; a transport failure raises the gRPC error. Wrap in begin/rescue.
  • Default timeout: read RPCs use the account's timeout (default 60 s).
  • Timestamps: server_time / server_time_utc are google.protobuf.Timestamp; read .seconds for unix seconds, or use the friendly MT5Service#account_info which returns numbers.
  • Session is automatic: connect obtains the terminal id and the SDK attaches it to this call — you never pass it yourself.

docs.title: 1) Basic usage
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt5"

acct = MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account.new("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443, api_key: ENV["MRPC_API_KEY"])
acct.connect(5057947437, "password", server: "MetaQuotes-Demo")

s = acct.account_summary
puts "Account Login: #{s.account_login}"
puts "Balance: #{s.account_balance.round(2)} #{s.account_currency}"
puts "Equity: #{s.account_equity.round(2)}"
puts "Leverage: 1:#{s.account_leverage}"

docs.title: 2) Compact status line for a CLI
docs.text:
def print_account_status(acct)
  s = acct.account_summary
  puts "Acc #{s.account_login} | #{s.account_currency} | " \
       "Bal #{s.account_balance.round(2)} | Eq #{s.account_equity.round(2)} | " \
       "Lev 1:#{s.account_leverage} | Mode #{trade_mode_to_s(s.account_trade_mode)}"
rescue MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError => e
  puts "❌ Error: #{e.message}"
end
# Output: Acc 5057947437 | USD | Bal 10000.0 | Eq 10050.25 | Lev 1:100 | Mode DEMO

docs.title: 3) Floating profit & margin health
docs.text:
def print_health(acct)
  s = acct.account_summary
  floating = s.account_equity - s.account_balance   # no dedicated profit field
  level = s.account_margin_level                    # 0 when flat

  puts "Floating P/L: #{floating.round(2)}"
  if level.zero?       then puts "No open margin"
  elsif level < 100    then puts "⚠️ Margin level critical!"
  elsif level < 200    then puts "⚠️ Low margin level"
  else                      puts "✅ Healthy margin level"
  end
end

docs.title: 4) Server time with timezone shift
docs.text:
def print_server_time(acct)
  s = acct.account_summary
  utc    = Time.at(s.server_time_utc.seconds).utc
  broker = Time.at(s.server_time.seconds).utc
  puts "Server time (UTC): #{utc.iso8601}"
  puts "Server time (broker): #{broker.iso8601}"
  puts "Broker offset from UTC: #{s.server_utc_offset_seconds} seconds"
end

docs.title: 5) Structured data model
docs.text:
AccountView = Struct.new(:login, :currency, :balance, :equity, :floating, :leverage, :trade_mode, :company, keyword_init: true)

def from_proto(s)
  AccountView.new(
    login: s.account_login, currency: s.account_currency,
    balance: s.account_balance, equity: s.account_equity,
    floating: s.account_equity - s.account_balance,
    leverage: s.account_leverage, trade_mode: trade_mode_to_s(s.account_trade_mode),
    company: s.account_company_name
  )
end

p from_proto(acct.account_summary)

docs.title: 6) Error handling
docs.text:
def try_get_summary(acct)
  acct.account_summary
rescue MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError, GRPC::BadStatus => e
  puts "Failed to get account summary: #{e.message}"
  nil
end

docs.title: Health check
docs.text:
def account_healthy?(acct)
  s = acct.account_summary
  s.account_login.positive? && !s.account_currency.empty? && s.account_leverage.positive?
rescue StandardError
  false
end

docs.title: Monitor account changes
docs.text:
def monitor_account(acct, interval_s)
  loop do
    s = acct.account_summary
    puts "[#{Time.now.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] Balance: #{s.account_balance.round(2)} | Equity: #{s.account_equity.round(2)}"
    sleep interval_s
  rescue MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError => e
    puts "❌ Error: #{e.message}"
  end
end
# Usage: monitor_account(acct, 5)

docs.title: MT5Account · Account Information — Overview
docs.text:
Account balance, equity, margin, leverage, currency, trade mode and server time — the complete snapshot in one call, or a single property at a time. Use this page to choose the right API for reading account state.

These methods are read-only. account_summary lives on mt5_term_api.AccountHelper; the account_info_* single-property methods on mt5_term_api.AccountInformation. Each returns the raw *Data (read fields with snake_case accessors), or raises ApiError.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text:
• AccountSummary — all account info at once (login, balance, equity, credit, leverage, currency, margin / free margin / margin level / margin mode, server time). Returns the MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode and MrpcEnumAccountMarginMode enums.
  • AccountInfoDouble — a single double property (balance, equity, margin, profit, credit…). Takes an AccountInfoDoublePropertyType.
  • AccountInfoInteger — a single integer property (login, leverage, limit orders…). Takes an AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType.
  • AccountInfoString — a single string property (name, server, currency, company). Takes an AccountInfoStringPropertyType.

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• account_summary → the one-stop shop for a complete snapshot. One RPC, everything you need for a dashboard, a pre-trade affordability check, or a connection heartbeat.
  • account_info_double / integer / string → grab one property when that's all you need — lighter than the full summary. Each takes a property enum selecting which value to read.

Rule of thumb: need the full snapshot → account_summary; need one specific value → account_info_*.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Enums used Complete account snapshot (all values) account_summary AccountSummaryData Output: MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode, MrpcEnumAccountMarginMode One numeric value (balance, equity, margin, …) account_info_double Float Input: AccountInfoDoublePropertyType One integer value (login, leverage, …) account_info_integer Integer Input: AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType One text value (currency, company, server, …) account_info_string String Input: AccountInfoStringPropertyType

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• Margin — account_summary already returns account_margin, account_margin_free, account_margin_level and account_margin_mode; account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE / :ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL) is just the single-value alternative.
  • Floating profit — the summary carries no dedicated profit field; compute account_equity − account_balance, or read account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_PROFIT).
  • Currency affects how profit is calculated — always check the account currency.
  • Leverage determines margin requirements — higher leverage, less margin needed.
  • Timeouts — read RPCs use the account's timeout (default 60 s); tune via acct.timeout = 30.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
# Complete account snapshot
s = acct.account_summary
puts "Balance: #{s.account_balance.round(2)}, Equity: #{s.account_equity.round(2)}, Leverage: 1:#{s.account_leverage}"

# Single property — account balance (pass the enum as a Ruby symbol)
balance = acct.account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_BALANCE)   # => Float
puts "Balance: #{balance.round(2)}"

# Single integer property — leverage
leverage = acct.account_info_integer(:ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE)
puts "Leverage: 1:#{leverage}"

# Single string property — currency
currency = acct.account_info_string(:ACCOUNT_CURRENCY)
puts "Currency: #{currency}"

# Account-health check — the summary already carries the margin level
s = acct.account_summary
level = s.account_margin_level   # also account_margin, account_margin_free

if level.positive? && level < 100      then puts "⚠️ Margin level critical!"
elsif level.positive? && level < 200   then puts "⚠️ Low margin level"
else                                        puts "✅ Healthy margin level"
end

docs.title: 🧱 Enums used in Account Information
docs.text: All four methods use enums — either as an input property selector, or as an output field describing the account. In Ruby, pass an enum as a symbol (:ACCOUNT_BALANCE); outputs come back as symbols too (:MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO).

docs.text:
Passed to the account_info_* methods to choose which property to read:

Method Input enum Purpose Example values account_info_double AccountInfoDoublePropertyType which double property :ACCOUNT_BALANCE, :ACCOUNT_EQUITY, :ACCOUNT_MARGIN, :ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE, :ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL, :ACCOUNT_PROFIT, :ACCOUNT_CREDIT, … (14 total) account_info_integer AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType which integer property :ACCOUNT_LOGIN, :ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE, :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE, :ACCOUNT_LIMIT_ORDERS, :ACCOUNT_TRADE_ALLOWED, :ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE, … (11 total) account_info_string AccountInfoStringPropertyType which string property :ACCOUNT_NAME, :ACCOUNT_SERVER, :ACCOUNT_CURRENCY, :ACCOUNT_COMPANY (4 total)

leverage = acct.account_info_integer(:ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE)
currency = acct.account_info_string(:ACCOUNT_CURRENCY)

docs.title: Output enums (returned values)
docs.text:
Returned in account_summary to describe account state:

Method Output enum Accessor Values account_summary MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode account_trade_mode :..._DEMO (0) · :..._CONTEST (1) · :..._REAL (2) account_summary MrpcEnumAccountMarginMode account_margin_mode :..._RETAIL_NETTING (0) · :..._EXCHANGE (1) · :..._RETAIL_HEDGING (2, typical MT5) 
s = acct.account_summary
case s.account_trade_mode
when :MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO then puts "Demo account"
when :MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_REAL then puts "Real account"
end

docs.title: 📝 Notes about enums
docs.text:
• Input enums are required — account_info_* always needs a property symbol.
  • Output enums are typed fields — account_summary returns account_trade_mode / account_margin_mode directly as symbols.
  • account_info_integer special case — some integer properties (e.g. :ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE) encode an enum, but come back as a plain Integer (0/1/2).
  • No enums on Double/String outputs — those always return a plain Float / String.

docs.title: ❓ Does a Symbol Exist?
docs.text:
Request: check whether a symbol is known to the server (SymbolExistData) — before you quote it, select it, or trade it.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbol_exist(symbol) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolExist (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolExist(SymbolExistRequest) → SymbolExistReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbol_exist(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that answers "does the server know this symbol name?"
  • Why you need it. Validate user input, guard a read/trade against a typo, filter a candidate list down to tradable names.
  • Sanity check. A known major like "EURUSD" returns true; a made-up name returns false (no error).

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
symbol_exist is your input-validation gate. It distinguishes "the symbol is wrong" (returns false) from "the call failed" (raises) — so you can reject bad input cleanly instead of letting a later symbol_info_tick / order_send blow up.

Exists ≠ ready. A symbol can exist yet not be selected in Market Watch or synchronized yet. For reads that need its data loaded, follow up with symbol_select and symbol_is_synchronized.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # True if the server knows `symbol`. Raises ApiError on a transport/gateway failure.
  def symbol_exist(symbol) -> Boolean
end

Request message: SymbolExistRequest { string name = 1; } Reply: the SDK returns data.exists (a Boolean).

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String The symbol name to check, e.g. "EURUSD".

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: true / false — whether the symbol exists on the server.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: a missing symbol is not an error (returns false); only transport/gateway failures raise ApiError.
  • Case & suffix sensitivity. Broker symbol names can carry suffixes (EURUSD.m, EURUSD-ECN). If false surprises you, list the catalog with acct.symbol_list and match the real spelling.
  • Exists vs selected vs synced — three different states; see SymbolSelect / SymbolIsSynchronized.

docs.title: 1) Guard a read
docs.text:
abort "unknown symbol" unless acct.symbol_exist("EURUSD")
t = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD")

docs.title: 2) Validate user input
docs.text:
def valid_symbol?(acct, name)
  acct.symbol_exist(name)
rescue MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError
  false
end

docs.title: 3) Filter a candidate list
docs.text:
wanted = %w[EURUSD FOOBAR GBPUSD XYZ]
tradable = wanted.select { |s| acct.symbol_exist(s) }
puts tradable.inspect   # => ["EURUSD", "GBPUSD"]

docs.title: 4) Resolve a suffix when the plain name misses
docs.text:
name = "EURUSD"
unless acct.symbol_exist(name)
  name = acct.symbol_list.find { |s| s.start_with?("EURUSD") } || name
end
puts name

docs.title: Ensure-and-select helper
docs.text:
def ensure_symbol(acct, sym)
  raise ArgumentError, "unknown symbol #{sym}" unless acct.symbol_exist(sym)
  acct.symbol_select(sym, true)
  sym
end

docs.title: 🔢 One Double Symbol Property
docs.text:
Request: a single floating-point symbol property (SymbolInfoDoubleData) — point, bid/ask, volume limits, tick value, swaps… — selected by an enum.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbol_info_double(symbol, property) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoDouble (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoDouble(SymbolInfoDoubleRequest) → SymbolInfoDoubleReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbol_info_double(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning a single Float symbol metric, chosen by a property enum.
  • Why you need it. Grab just one number — the point size for pip math, the min lot for sizing, the tick value for risk — without pulling the whole spec.
  • Sanity check. symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_POINT) is a small positive number (e.g. 1.0e-05).

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: Read one double property when that's all you need. For many values at once, symbol_params_many returns the full SymbolParameters in a single call — cheaper than many single reads.

docs.title: 1) Point & lot limits
docs.text:

puts "1 pip = #{pip}"

API Information:

docs.text:

  • Method: SymbolInfoInteger(SymbolInfoIntegerRequest) → SymbolInfoIntegerReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning a single Integer symbol property, chosen by a property enum.
  • Why you need it. The two you'll reach for most: :SYMBOL_DIGITS (how many decimals to round prices to) and :SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL (the minimum SL/TP distance).
  • Sanity check. symbol_info_integer("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_DIGITS) is 5 on most 5-digit FX feeds.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: Read one integer property on demand. :SYMBOL_DIGITS and :SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL are the pre-trade essentials — round prices to the right precision and keep SL/TP outside the freeze/stops distance so orders aren't rejected.

SYMBOL_FILLING_MODE          = 32   // allowed filling modes bitmask
SYMBOL_ORDER_MODE            = 33
SYMBOL_ORDER_GTC_MODE        = 34
SYMBOL_OPTION_MODE           = 35
SYMBOL_OPTION_RIGHT          = 36

Result enums: :SYMBOL_SECTOR and :SYMBOL_INDUSTRY return a code (a plain Integer) from BMT5_ENUM_SYMBOL_SECTOR / BMT5_ENUM_SYMBOL_INDUSTRY — map it yourself, or read the already-typed SymbolParameters.sector / .industry from symbol_params_many. See the ENUMs Reference.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • :SYMBOL_DIGITS → how many decimals to round prices to before sending an order.
  • :SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL → the minimum SL/TP distance in points; orders inside it are rejected.
  • Boolean-ish flags (:SYMBOL_VISIBLE, :SYMBOL_SELECT) come back as 0/1.

docs.title: 1) Digits & stops level
docs.text:
digits = acct.symbol_info_integer("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_DIGITS)
stops  = acct.symbol_info_integer("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL)
puts "digits #{digits}  min stop #{stops} pts"

docs.title: 2) Round a price to the symbol's digits
docs.text:
digits = acct.symbol_info_integer("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_DIGITS)
price  = 1.0942371
puts price.round(digits)

docs.title: 3) Validate an SL distance before sending
docs.text:
pt    = acct.symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_POINT)
stops = acct.symbol_info_integer("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL)
bid   = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD").bid
sl    = bid - 300 * pt
ok    = (bid - sl) >= stops * pt
puts ok ? "SL ok" : "SL too close (min #{stops} pts)"

docs.title: 4) Is the symbol visible?
docs.text: puts acct.symbol_info_integer("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_VISIBLE) == 1 ? "visible" : "hidden"

docs.title: Price-rounding helper
docs.text:
def round_price(acct, sym, price)
  price.round(acct.symbol_info_integer(sym, :SYMBOL_DIGITS))
end

docs.text:

  • Friendly layer: MT5Sugar#symbol_digits / #min_stop_level.

docs.title: 🔤 One String Symbol Property
docs.text:
Request: a single text symbol property (SymbolInfoStringData) — description, base/profit/margin currency, path… — selected by an enum.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbol_info_string(symbol, property) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoString (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoString(SymbolInfoStringRequest) → SymbolInfoStringReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbol_info_string(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning a single String symbol property, chosen by a property enum.
  • Why you need it. Read the human description for a UI, or the base/profit currencies that drive profit & margin math.
  • Sanity check. symbol_info_string("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_CURRENCY_BASE) is "EUR".

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: Read one text property on demand — most often the currencies (which decide how profit and margin are calculated) or a description for display.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # One SYMBOL_* string property. `property` is a SymbolInfoStringProperty symbol.
  def symbol_info_string(symbol, property) -> String
end

Request message: SymbolInfoStringRequest { string symbol = 1; SymbolInfoStringProperty type = 2; } Reply: the SDK returns data.value (a String).

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String The symbol, e.g. "EURUSD". property Symbol (SymbolInfoStringProperty) Which string property to read.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: A single String.

docs.title: 🧱 Property enum — SymbolInfoStringProperty (all 15 values)
docs.text:
Pass any of these as the property symbol (e.g. :SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION):

SYMBOL_BASIS           = 0
SYMBOL_CATEGORY        = 1
SYMBOL_COUNTRY         = 2
SYMBOL_SECTOR_NAME     = 3    // economic sector name
SYMBOL_INDUSTRY_NAME   = 4    // industry / activity name
SYMBOL_CURRENCY_BASE   = 5    // base currency (EUR for EURUSD)
SYMBOL_CURRENCY_PROFIT = 6    // profit currency (USD for EURUSD)
SYMBOL_CURRENCY_MARGIN = 7    // margin currency
SYMBOL_BANK            = 8
SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION     = 9    // human-readable description ("Euro vs US Dollar")
SYMBOL_EXCHANGE        = 10
SYMBOL_FORMULA         = 11   // formula for a custom/synthetic symbol
SYMBOL_ISIN            = 12   // ISIN (where available)
SYMBOL_PAGE            = 13   // web page URL
SYMBOL_PATH            = 14   // Market Watch tree path

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • Currencies matter. If the profit currency isn't the account currency, P/L is converted at the current rate — expect small differences vs a naive points×value estimate.
  • One call for everything: the same fields live on SymbolParameters (currency_base, currency_profit, sym_description, path) via symbol_params_many.

docs.title: 1) Description for a UI
docs.text: puts acct.symbol_info_string("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION)   # "Euro vs US Dollar"

docs.title: 2) Base / profit currency
docs.text:
base   = acct.symbol_info_string("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_CURRENCY_BASE)
profit = acct.symbol_info_string("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_CURRENCY_PROFIT)
puts "#{base} → #{profit}"

docs.title: 3) Is profit in the account currency?
docs.text:
acct_ccy = acct.account_info_string(:ACCOUNT_CURRENCY)
sym_ccy  = acct.symbol_info_string("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_CURRENCY_PROFIT)
puts sym_ccy == acct_ccy ? "no conversion" : "converted #{sym_ccy}→#{acct_ccy}"

docs.title: 4) Market-Watch folder
docs.text: puts acct.symbol_info_string("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_PATH)   # e.g. "Forex\\Majors\\EURUSD"

docs.title: Display label
docs.text:
def symbol_label(acct, sym)
  "#{sym} — #{acct.symbol_info_string(sym, :SYMBOL_DESCRIPTION)}"
end

docs.title: 📈 Getting the Latest Tick
docs.text:
Request: the most recent tick for a symbol (MrpcMqlTick) — bid, ask, last, volume and timestamps. This is where prices come from.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbol_info_tick(symbol) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoTick (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoTick(SymbolInfoTickRequest) → SymbolInfoTickReply

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning the latest quote for a symbol.
  • Why you need it. Current bid/ask before trading, spread monitoring, a lightweight price feed (poll it, or use the on_symbol_tick stream for push).
  • Sanity check. bid and ask are non-zero on an active symbol; ask > bid.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # Latest tick for `symbol`. Returns MrpcMqlTick; raises ApiError on failure.
  def symbol_info_tick(symbol) -> Mt5TermApi::MrpcMqlTick
end

Request message: SymbolInfoTickRequest { string symbol = 1; } Reply: SymbolInfoTickReply { oneof response { MrpcMqlTick data; Error error; } } — the SDK returns data.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String The symbol, e.g. "EURUSD". Required.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — MrpcMqlTick
docs.text:
Field Ruby accessor Type Description bid bid Float Best bid price. ask ask Float Best ask price. last last Float Last deal price (often 0 on FX). volume volume Integer Tick volume. volume_real volume_real Float Real volume (exchange symbols). time time Integer Tick time, unix seconds (broker tz). time_utc time_utc Integer Tick time, unix seconds (UTC). time_msc time_msc Integer Tick time in milliseconds (broker tz). time_msc_utc time_msc_utc Integer Tick time in milliseconds (UTC). flags flags Integer Tick flags bitmask (which fields changed).

Spread = ask - bid (price units). In points: ((ask - bid) / point).round, where point = symbol_info_double(symbol, :SYMBOL_POINT).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError; wrap in begin/rescue.
  • last is 0 on FX — use bid / ask for quotes.
  • Push vs poll: for a live feed use on_symbol_tick instead of polling this in a loop.
  • Select first if a symbol isn't loaded: symbol_select(symbol, true).

docs.title: 1) Current quote & spread
docs.text:
t = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD")
spread_pts = ((t.ask - t.bid) / acct.symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_POINT)).round
puts "bid #{t.bid}  ask #{t.ask}  spread #{spread_pts} pts"

docs.title: 2) Tick age
docs.text:
t = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD")
age = Time.now.utc.to_i - t.time_utc
puts "last tick #{age}s ago"

docs.title: 3) Poll a few symbols
docs.text:
%w[EURUSD GBPUSD USDJPY].each do |sym|
  t = acct.symbol_info_tick(sym)
  puts format("%-8s %s / %s", sym, t.bid, t.ask)
end

docs.text:

  • OnSymbolTick — push stream of ticks.
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service#quote → Quote(bid, ask, last, spread, time_utc).

docs.title: 🔄 Is a Symbol Synchronized?
docs.text:
Request: whether the terminal has finished syncing a symbol's data with the server (SymbolIsSynchronizedData) — the "ready to read" signal.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbol_is_synchronized(symbol) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolIsSynchronized (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolIsSynchronized(SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest) → SymbolIsSynchronizedReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbol_is_synchronized(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC telling you if symbol's specs/quotes/history are in sync with the broker.
  • Why you need it. Right after symbol_select, a symbol may not be ready — gate your reads on this.
  • Sanity check. A long-selected major reads true; a just-selected exotic may read false for a moment.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: symbol_is_synchronized is the "is it ready?" check in the symbol lifecycle (exist? → select → synchronized? → read). Polling it before reading history or specs avoids stale/empty data on freshly selected symbols.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def symbol_is_synchronized(symbol) -> Boolean
end

Request message: SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest { string symbol = 1; } Reply: the SDK returns data.synchronized (a Boolean).

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String The symbol name.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: true when the symbol's specs/history are synchronized.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • Poll, don't assume. After symbol_select a symbol can read false briefly — loop with a small sleep and a timeout.
  • Pairs with sync-sensitive reads — price_history family and symbol_params_many are the ones most worth gating.

docs.title: 1) One-shot check
docs.text: puts acct.symbol_is_synchronized("EURUSD")

docs.title: 2) Wait until ready (with timeout)
docs.text:
deadline = Time.now + 5
sleep 0.2 until acct.symbol_is_synchronized("XAUUSD") || Time.now > deadline

docs.title: 3) Select then confirm
docs.text:
acct.symbol_select("GBPUSD", true)
puts acct.symbol_is_synchronized("GBPUSD") ? "ready" : "still syncing"

docs.title: 4) Only read when synced
docs.text:
if acct.symbol_is_synchronized("EURUSD")
  bars = acct.price_history("EURUSD", timeframe: :H1, max_bars: 100)
end

docs.title: Block until synchronized
docs.text:
def wait_synced(acct, sym, timeout: 5)
  deadline = Time.now + timeout
  until acct.symbol_is_synchronized(sym)
    raise "sync timeout for #{sym}" if Time.now > deadline
    sleep 0.2
  end
end

docs.text:
• SymbolSelect · SymbolExist
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service#symbol_synchronized?.

docs.title: 🔤 Symbol Name by Index
docs.text:
Request: the name of the symbol at a given index (SymbolNameData) — walk the catalog, or the Market-Watch subset, position by position.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbol_name(index, selected: false) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolName (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolName(SymbolNameRequest) → SymbolNameReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbol_name(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning the symbol name at position index — over the full catalog, or only the Market-Watch list.
  • Why you need it. Iterate the catalog with symbols_total, build a picker, or read the n-th Market-Watch symbol.
  • Sanity check. symbol_name(0) returns a real name; an out-of-range index raises.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
symbol_name is the index → name half of catalog iteration (symbols_total gives you the count). Together they let you enumerate symbols without hard-coding names.

Prefer the whole list? acct.symbol_list returns every name in one call — cheaper than looping symbol_name across thousands of indices. Use symbol_name when you need a single position (e.g. "the first Market-Watch symbol") or are streaming through a huge catalog lazily.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # Name of the symbol at `index`. selected: true indexes within Market Watch only.
  def symbol_name(index, selected: false) -> String
end

Request message: SymbolNameRequest { int32 index = 1; bool selected = 2; } Reply: the SDK returns data.name (a String).

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description index Integer Zero-based index into the symbol list. selected Boolean (keyword, default false) false = index into the full catalog; true = index into Market-Watch symbols only.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: A String — the symbol name at that index.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: an out-of-range index raises ApiError — bound your loop with symbols_total.
  • Two index spaces. selected: false and selected: true are different orderings and sizes — pick the one that matches your count.
  • N round-trips. Looping symbol_name over the whole catalog is one call per index; acct.symbol_list is one call total.

docs.title: 1) First symbol (catalog vs Market Watch)
docs.text:
puts "catalog[0]      #{acct.symbol_name(0)}"
puts "market_watch[0] #{acct.symbol_name(0, selected: true)}"

docs.title: 2) First 5 names
docs.text: (0...5).each { |i| puts acct.symbol_name(i) }

docs.title: 3) Safely read the n-th Market-Watch symbol
docs.text:
def mw_symbol(acct, i)
  i < acct.symbols_total(mode: true) ? acct.symbol_name(i, selected: true) : nil
end

docs.title: 4) Build the list (prefer symbol_list)
docs.text:
total = acct.symbols_total
names = (0...total).map { |i| acct.symbol_name(i) }   # heavier
# names = acct.symbol_list                             # one call — preferred

docs.title: Paginated picker
docs.text:
def page_symbols(acct, page:, per: 20)
  start = page * per
  stop  = [start + per, acct.symbols_total].min
  (start...stop).map { |i| acct.symbol_name(i) }
end

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• SymbolsTotal — the count · SymbolExist — existence.
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service#symbol_name / #symbols.

docs.title: ➕ Show / Hide a Symbol in Market Watch
docs.text:
Request: add or remove a symbol from Market Watch (SymbolSelectData). Some reads require a symbol to be selected before its data is available.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbol_select(symbol, select = true) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolSelect (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolSelect(SymbolSelectRequest) → SymbolSelectReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbol_select(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC that toggles a symbol in Market Watch — select = true shows it, false hides it.
  • Why you need it. The terminal only keeps live data for selected symbols; select an uncommon one before quoting, reading its spec, or trading it.
  • Sanity check. symbol_select("EURUSD", true) returns true; right after, symbol_is_synchronized flips to true.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
symbol_select warms up a symbol. Majors are usually selected already, but a symbol the terminal hasn't loaded needs this first — otherwise symbol_info_tick / symbol_params_many may return stale or empty data.

Lifecycle: symbol_exist? → symbol_select(true) → wait for symbol_is_synchronized → read. Hide it again with symbol_select(false) when you're done, to keep Market Watch tidy.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # Add (select=true) or remove (select=false) `symbol` from Market Watch.
  def symbol_select(symbol, select = true) -> Boolean
end

Request message: SymbolSelectRequest { string symbol = 1; bool select = 2; } Reply: the SDK returns data.success (a Boolean).

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String The symbol name. select Boolean (default true) true = show in Market Watch, false = hide.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: true on success.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure; wrap in begin/rescue.
  • Call it before reading ticks/params for a symbol the terminal hasn't loaded.
  • You can't remove a symbol that has open positions or pending orders — hide will fail.
  • Not instant. After selecting, poll symbol_is_synchronized before relying on history/specs.

docs.title: 1) Select, then quote
docs.text:
acct.symbol_select("GBPUSD", true)
t = acct.symbol_info_tick("GBPUSD")
puts "#{t.bid}/#{t.ask}"

docs.title: 2) Select and wait until synced
docs.text:
acct.symbol_select("XAUUSD", true)
sleep 0.2 until acct.symbol_is_synchronized("XAUUSD")
puts "ready"

docs.title: 3) Hide when done
docs.text: acct.symbol_select("GBPUSD", false)

docs.title: 4) Bulk-select a basket
docs.text: %w[EURUSD GBPUSD USDJPY].each { |s| acct.symbol_select(s, true) }

docs.title: Ensure-ready helper
docs.text:
def ensure_ready(acct, sym, timeout: 5)
  acct.symbol_select(sym, true)
  deadline = Time.now + timeout
  sleep 0.2 until acct.symbol_is_synchronized(sym) || Time.now > deadline
  sym
end

  • Friendly layer: MT5Service#select_symbol.

docs.title: MT5Account · Symbol Information — Overview
docs.text:
Live quotes, symbol properties and Market-Watch management. Read a tick, a single symbol property, or check existence / sync state — all on mt5_term_api.MarketInfo.

These methods are read-only except symbol_select (which toggles a symbol in Market Watch). Each returns the raw *Data (snake_case accessors) or a plain value, or raises ApiError.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text: Method What it does SymbolsTotal count of symbols (all, or Market-Watch only) SymbolExist does a symbol exist on the server? SymbolName symbol name by index SymbolSelect add / remove a symbol from Market Watch SymbolIsSynchronized is the symbol's data synced with the server? SymbolInfoDouble one SYMBOL_* double property (point, volume_min…) SymbolInfoInteger one SYMBOL_* integer property (digits, spread…) SymbolInfoString one SYMBOL_* string property (description, base currency…) SymbolInfoTick the latest tick (bid / ask / last / time)

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• Prices come from symbol_info_tick — not from the symbol spec. For the full contract spec in one call use symbol_params_many.
  • symbol_info_double / integer / string read one property at a time (point, digits, stops level, currencies…).
  • symbol_select(sym, true) makes a symbol visible in Market Watch — required before some reads on symbols the terminal hasn't loaded yet.

Rule of thumb: need a price → symbol_info_tick; need one property → symbol_info_*; need the whole spec → symbol_params_many.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Bid / ask / last right now symbol_info_tick MrpcMqlTick How many symbols exist symbols_total Integer Whether a symbol exists symbol_exist Boolean A symbol name by index symbol_name String Show/hide in Market Watch symbol_select Boolean Sync state symbol_is_synchronized Boolean One numeric property symbol_info_double Float One integer property symbol_info_integer Integer One text property symbol_info_string String

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• symbol_info_tick.last is often 0 on FX — use bid / ask.
  • Select before reading uncommon symbols: symbol_select(sym) then read.
  • Pip vs point: on 5/3-digit symbols a pip = 10 × point. point comes from symbol_info_double(:SYMBOL_POINT).
  • Full spec (lot limits, stops level, currencies) → symbol_params_many is one call for everything.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
t = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD")
puts "bid #{t.bid}  ask #{t.ask}  spread #{(t.ask - t.bid).round(5)}"

digits = acct.symbol_info_integer("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_DIGITS)
point  = acct.symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_POINT)
puts "digits #{digits}  point #{point}"

acct.symbol_select("GBPUSD", true)          # ensure it's in Market Watch
puts "exists? #{acct.symbol_exist('GBPUSD')}  synced? #{acct.symbol_is_synchronized('GBPUSD')}"

docs.text:

docs.title: 🔢 Counting Symbols
docs.text:
Request: how many symbols the terminal knows (SymbolsTotalData) — all of them, or only those currently in Market Watch.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbols_total(mode: false) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolsTotal (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolsTotal(SymbolsTotalRequest) → SymbolsTotalReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbols_total(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning the number of symbols — the whole broker catalog, or just the ones shown in Market Watch.
  • Why you need it. Size a loop over symbol_name, show "N instruments available", or check how many symbols are selected vs hidden.
  • Sanity check. The all-symbols count (mode: false) is ≥ the Market-Watch count (mode: true), and both are > 0 once connected.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
Use it whenever you need the size of the symbol universe rather than the names themselves:

  • Bound an index loop with symbol_name(i).
  • Report catalog size in a dashboard or health check.
  • Measure how many symbols are in Market Watch vs the full list (hidden = all − selected).

Just want every name? acct.symbol_list returns the full [String] in one call — no need to loop symbol_name yourself.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # Count of symbols. mode: true counts only Market-Watch (selected) symbols.
  # Returns an Integer; raises ApiError on failure.
  def symbols_total(mode: false) -> Integer
end

Request message: SymbolsTotalRequest { bool mode = 1; } Reply: SymbolsTotalReply { oneof response { SymbolsTotalData data; Error error; } } — the SDK returns data.total.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description mode Boolean (keyword, default false) false = all symbols on the server; true = only those in Market Watch.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: A single Integer — the number of symbols.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError on a server rejection; wrap in begin/rescue.
  • Big catalogs. A broker can expose 10k+ symbols (mode: false); don't eagerly fetch a tick/spec for every one — select and read only what you trade.
  • Market Watch is smaller. mode: true reflects what's currently selected; grow it with symbol_select.
  • Names, not just the count: iterate with symbol_name, or get them all at once via acct.symbol_list.

docs.title: 1) All vs Market Watch
docs.text:
all = acct.symbols_total
mw  = acct.symbols_total(mode: true)
puts "catalog #{all}  ·  market watch #{mw}  ·  hidden #{all - mw}"

docs.title: 2) Iterate the first N symbols
docs.text:
n = [acct.symbols_total, 10].min
(0...n).each { |i| puts acct.symbol_name(i) }

docs.title: 3) Health check — is the catalog loaded?
docs.text:
def catalog_ready?(acct)
  acct.symbols_total.positive?
rescue MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError
  false
end

docs.title: 4) Market-Watch ratio
docs.text:
all = acct.symbols_total.to_f
pct = all.zero? ? 0 : (100 * acct.symbols_total(mode: true) / all).round(1)
puts "#{pct}% of symbols are in Market Watch"

docs.title: Build a symbol index (prefer symbol_list)
docs.text:
# Cheapest: one call for every name
names = acct.symbol_list                      # => [String]

# Or, if you specifically need the count first:
total = acct.symbols_total
names = (0...total).map { |i| acct.symbol_name(i) }   # heavier: N round-trips

docs.text:

  • SymbolSelect — grow Market Watch.
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service#symbols_total / #symbols.

docs.title: 📂 Open Positions & Pending Orders
docs.text:
Request: everything open right now (OpenedOrdersData) — filled positions and working orders — in one call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#opened_orders(sort:) · gRPC: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper · Proto: OpenedOrders

docs.title: RPC
docs.text: OpenedOrders(OpenedOrdersRequest) → OpenedOrdersReply — the SDK returns data (OpenedOrdersData).

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning open positions (position_infos) and pending orders (opened_orders).
  • Why you need it. Build a live book, compute exposure, find a ticket to modify/close.
  • Sanity check. position_infos.size matches positions_total.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # Open positions + pending orders. sort: a BMT5_OPENED_ORDER_SORT_* symbol.
  def opened_orders(sort: :BMT5_OPENED_ORDER_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC) -> Mt5TermApi::OpenedOrdersData
end

Request message: OpenedOrdersRequest { EnumOpenedOrderSortType inputSortMode = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description sort Symbol (keyword) Ordering, e.g. :BMT5_OPENED_ORDER_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC.

docs.title: 🧱 Sort enum — BMT5_ENUM_OPENED_ORDER_SORT_TYPE (all 4)
docs.text:
BMT5_OPENED_ORDER_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC        = 0
BMT5_OPENED_ORDER_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC       = 1
BMT5_OPENED_ORDER_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_ASC  = 2
BMT5_OPENED_ORDER_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_DESC = 3

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OpenedOrdersData
docs.text:
• position_infos → [PositionInfo] — filled positions.
  • opened_orders → [] — pending / working orders.

docs.title: PositionInfo (key fields)

The enum-typed fields on each returned row come back as Ruby symbols:

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError.
  • Filter in Ruby by magic_number / symbol, or use MT5Service#positions(magic:, symbol:).
  • Lightweight alternative: opened_orders_tickets when you only need ids.

docs.title: 1) List open positions
docs.text:
acct.opened_orders.position_infos.each do |p|
  puts format("#%d %-8s %s %.2f @ %s  P/L %.2f", p.ticket, p.symbol, p.type, p.volume, p.price_open, p.profit)
end

docs.title: 2) Total exposure by symbol
docs.text:
by_sym = Hash.new(0.0)
acct.opened_orders.position_infos.each { |p| by_sym[p.symbol] += p.volume }
p by_sym

docs.title: 3) Find a ticket to close
docs.text:
pos = acct.opened_orders.position_infos.find { |p| p.symbol == "EURUSD" }
acct.order_close(ticket: pos.ticket) if pos

docs.title: 🎫 Open Tickets (Lightweight)
docs.text:
Request: just the tickets of open positions and pending orders (OpenedOrdersTicketsData) — no per-order detail, ideal for cheap diffs.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#opened_orders_tickets (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: OpenedOrdersTickets (defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: OpenedOrdersTickets(OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest) → OpenedOrdersTicketsReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::AccountHelper::Stub#opened_orders_tickets(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning two id lists: open position tickets and pending order tickets.
  • Why you need it. Detect opens/closes by diffing successive snapshots, without transferring full order payloads.
  • Sanity check. opened_position_tickets.size matches positions_total.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: opened_orders_tickets is the change-detection primitive. Poll it on a timer (or use the on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets stream), keep the previous set, and the set difference tells you exactly what opened or closed — far cheaper than re-pulling opened_orders each time.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def opened_orders_tickets -> Mt5TermApi::OpenedOrdersTicketsData
end

Request message: OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {} (empty). Reply: the SDK returns data (OpenedOrdersTicketsData).

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: None.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OpenedOrdersTicketsData
docs.text:
Field Ruby accessor Type Description opened_position_tickets opened_position_tickets Integer[] Tickets of open positions. opened_orders_tickets opened_orders_tickets Integer[] Tickets of pending/working orders.

Both are repeated fields — call .to_a to get a plain Ruby array.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • Much lighter than opened_orders — use it when you only need ids.
  • Diff with Set operations: (current - previous) = newly opened; (previous - current) = just closed.

docs.title: 1) Count cheaply
docs.text:
tk = acct.opened_orders_tickets
puts "positions #{tk.opened_position_tickets.to_a.size}  pending #{tk.opened_orders_tickets.to_a.size}"

docs.title: 2) Detect new opens (diff two snapshots)
docs.text:
before = acct.opened_orders_tickets.opened_position_tickets.to_a
# ... place a trade elsewhere ...
after  = acct.opened_orders_tickets.opened_position_tickets.to_a
puts "newly opened: #{(after - before).inspect}"

docs.title: 3) Pending-order ids
docs.text: p acct.opened_orders_tickets.opened_orders_tickets.to_a

docs.title: 4) Is a specific ticket still open?
docs.text:
open = acct.opened_orders_tickets.opened_position_tickets.to_a
puts open.include?(123_456) ? "still open" : "closed"

docs.title: Poll for closes
docs.text:
def wait_closed(acct, ticket, timeout: 30)
  deadline = Time.now + timeout
  loop do
    return true unless acct.opened_orders_tickets.opened_position_tickets.to_a.include?(ticket)
    return false if Time.now > deadline
    sleep 0.5
  end
end

docs.text:

  • OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets — push version.
  • Friendly layer: MT5Sugar#open_tickets.

docs.title: 📜 Order & Deal History
docs.text:
Request: closed orders and deals in a time window ([HistoryData]). The SDK auto-pages the gateway and returns the full list.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#order_history(from_utc:, to_utc:, sort:, page_size:) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderHistory (defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: OrderHistory(OrderHistoryRequest) → OrderHistoryReply
  • Low-level client (generated): the SDK loops pages via next_page_token and concatenates data.history_data.

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Historical orders + deals between two UTC times, fully paged for you.
  • Why you need it. P/L reports, trade journals, reconciliation against your own records.
  • Sanity check. Each HistoryData carries a history_order and/or history_deal.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: order_history is the audit trail at order/deal grain. One order can produce several deals (partial fills), so iterate history_deal for realized money. For a simpler "one row per round-trip" view, use positions_history instead.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def order_history(from_utc:, to_utc: Time.now.utc,
                    sort: :BMT5_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_ASC, page_size: 500) -> Array
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description from_utc Time / Integer (keyword, required) Window start (UTC). to_utc Time / Integer (keyword) Window end (UTC). Default: now. sort Symbol (keyword) Ordering, e.g. :BMT5_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_ASC. page_size Integer (keyword) Page size for the internal paging loop.

docs.title: 🧱 Sort enum — BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_HISTORY_SORT_TYPE (all 6)
docs.text:
BMT5_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_ASC        = 0
BMT5_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC       = 1
BMT5_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_ASC       = 2
BMT5_SORT_BY_CLOSE_TIME_DESC      = 3
BMT5_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_ASC  = 4
BMT5_SORT_BY_ORDER_TICKET_ID_DESC = 5

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text:
An Array of HistoryData. Each item exposes:

  • history_order — the order record (type, volume, prices, times).
  • history_deal — the executed deal: ticket, symbol, volume, price, profit, commission, swap, time.

docs.title: 🧱 Enum values (outputs)
docs.text:
Each history row (OrderHistoryData) is an order — its enum fields as symbols:

type → BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE 
BMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY = 0   BMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL = 1
BMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_LIMIT = 2   BMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_LIMIT = 3
BMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP = 4   BMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP = 5
BMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP_LIMIT = 6   BMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP_LIMIT = 7   BMT5_ORDER_TYPE_CLOSE_BY = 8
state → BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_STATE 
BMT5_ORDER_STATE_STARTED = 0   BMT5_ORDER_STATE_PLACED = 1   BMT5_ORDER_STATE_CANCELED = 2
BMT5_ORDER_STATE_PARTIAL = 3   BMT5_ORDER_STATE_FILLED = 4   BMT5_ORDER_STATE_REJECTED = 5
BMT5_ORDER_STATE_EXPIRED = 6   BMT5_ORDER_STATE_REQUEST_ADD = 7
BMT5_ORDER_STATE_REQUEST_MODIFY = 8   BMT5_ORDER_STATE_REQUEST_CANCEL = 9
type_filling → BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_FILLING 
BMT5_ORDER_FILLING_FOK = 0   BMT5_ORDER_FILLING_IOC = 1   BMT5_ORDER_FILLING_RETURN = 2   BMT5_ORDER_FILLING_BOC = 3
type_time → BMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TIME 
BMT5_ORDER_TIME_GTC = 0   BMT5_ORDER_TIME_DAY = 1   BMT5_ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED = 2   BMT5_ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED_DAY = 3

order_history returns orders only (no deal rows), so no deal-type/entry/reason enums appear here.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError. Uses a longer internal deadline (history can be large).
  • UTC times: pass Time objects; the SDK builds the protobuf Timestamps.
  • Deals vs orders: one order → several deals (partial fills); sum history_deal.profit for realized P/L.
  • Big windows: keep page_size reasonable (default 500) — the SDK still returns the full concatenated array.

docs.title: 1) Last 7 days of deals
docs.text:
from = Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600
acct.order_history(from_utc: from).each do |h|
  d = h.history_deal
  next unless d
  puts format("deal #%d  %-8s  vol %.2f  price %s  profit %.2f", d.ticket, d.symbol, d.volume, d.price, d.profit)
end

docs.title: 2) Total realized P/L
docs.text:
total = acct.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600)
            .filter_map { |h| h.history_deal&.profit }.sum
puts "30-day realized P/L: #{total.round(2)}"

docs.title: 3) A specific calendar window
docs.text: acct.order_history(from_utc: Time.utc(2025, 1, 1), to_utc: Time.utc(2025, 2, 1))

docs.title: 4) Per-symbol realized P/L
docs.text:
by_sym = Hash.new(0.0)
acct.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600).each do |h|
  d = h.history_deal or next
  by_sym[d.symbol] += d.profit
end
p by_sym

docs.title: Daily P/L buckets
docs.text:
def daily_pl(acct, days: 7)
  acct.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - days * 24 * 3600)
      .filter_map { |h| h.history_deal }
      .group_by   { |d| Time.at(d.time.seconds).utc.to_date rescue nil }
      .transform_values { |ds| ds.sum(&:profit).round(2) }
end

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• PositionsHistory — one row per closed round-trip.
  • Friendly layer: MT5Sugar#order_history · MT5Service#order_history.

docs.title: MT5Account · Positions & Orders — Overview
docs.text:
Open positions, pending orders, their tickets, and the closed history. In MT5 a position is net market exposure, an order is a pending/working instruction, and a deal is an executed transaction recorded in history.

Reads live on mt5_term_api.AccountHelper / TradeFunctions. Each returns the raw *Data or a plain value, or raises ApiError.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text: Method What it does PositionsTotal count of open positions OpenedOrders open positions and pending orders, full detail OpenedOrdersTickets just the tickets (lightweight) OrderHistory closed orders + deals in a time window (auto-paged) PositionsHistory closed positions / round-trips (auto-paged)

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• Now: opened_orders gives you both open positions (position_infos) and pending orders (opened_orders) in one reply; positions_total is just the count; opened_orders_tickets is the cheap tickets-only variant.
  • History: order_history returns closed orders & deals; positions_history returns one row per closed round-trip (open→close, with profit).

Rule of thumb: what's open now → opened_orders; what happened before → order_history / positions_history.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns How many positions are open positions_total Integer Open positions + pending orders opened_orders OpenedOrdersData Only the tickets opened_orders_tickets OpenedOrdersTicketsData Closed orders & deals (window) order_history [HistoryData] Closed round-trips (window) positions_history [PositionHistoryInfo]

docs.title: ❌ Cross-refs & gotchas
docs.text:
• History takes UTC times — pass Time objects (the SDK converts to protobuf Timestamps). History reads are auto-paged by the SDK.
  • Position ≠ order. opened_orders.position_infos are filled positions; opened_orders.opened_orders are pending/working orders.
  • Filter in Ruby — opened_orders.position_infos.select { |p| p.magic_number == 600001 }, or use MT5Service#positions(magic:, symbol:).

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
data = acct.opened_orders
puts "positions #{data.position_infos.size}  pending #{data.opened_orders.size}"
data.position_infos.each { |p| puts "##{p.ticket} #{p.symbol} #{p.volume} P/L #{p.profit}" }

from = Time.now.utc - 7*24*3600
acct.order_history(from_utc: from).last(5).each { |h| puts h.history_deal&.ticket }

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Trading: Trading Operations — Overview — place / modify / close.
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service#positions / #order_history.

docs.title: 📘 Positions History (Round-Trips)
docs.text:
Request: closed positions — one row per round-trip ([PositionHistoryInfo]), with open/close prices and realized profit. The SDK auto-pages and returns the full list.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#positions_history(from_utc:, to_utc:, sort:, page_size:) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: PositionsHistory (defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: PositionsHistory(PositionsHistoryRequest) → PositionsHistoryReply
  • Low-level client (generated): the SDK loops pages via next_page_token and concatenates data.history_positions.

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Closed positions, one row per round-trip (open → close), with realized profit.
  • Why you need it. Win-rate, equity curve, best/worst trades — the simplest view of trading results.
  • Sanity check. Rows have a position_ticket, symbol, profit, and open/close prices.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: positions_history is the results read. Where order_history is order/deal grained (one order → several deals), this gives you one tidy row per completed position — ideal for performance stats.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def positions_history(from_utc:, to_utc: Time.now.utc,
                        sort: :AH_POSITION_OPEN_TIME_ASC, page_size: 500) -> Array
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description from_utc Time / Integer (keyword, required) Window start (UTC) — filters by position open time. to_utc Time / Integer (keyword) Window end (UTC). Default: now. sort Symbol (keyword) Ordering, e.g. :AH_POSITION_OPEN_TIME_ASC. page_size Integer (keyword) Page size for the internal paging loop.

docs.title: 🧱 Sort enum — AH_ENUM_POSITIONS_HISTORY_SORT_TYPE (all 4)
docs.text:
AH_POSITION_OPEN_TIME_ASC  = 0
AH_POSITION_OPEN_TIME_DESC = 1
AH_POSITION_TICKET_ASC     = 2
AH_POSITION_TICKET_DESC    = 3

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — [PositionHistoryInfo]
docs.text: Field Ruby accessor Type Description position_ticket position_ticket Integer Position ticket (note: not ticket). symbol symbol String Symbol. order_type order_type Symbol Direction (buy / sell) enum. volume volume Float Volume in lots. open_price / close_price open_price / close_price Float Entry / exit price. open_time / close_time open_time / close_time Timestamp Open / close time. profit profit Float Realized profit. swap / commission / fee swap / commission / fee Float Costs. magic magic Integer EA magic number. comment comment String Comment.

docs.title: order_type → AH_ENUM_POSITIONS_HISTORY_ORDER_TYPE
docs.text:
The direction that opened each closed position, as a symbol:

AH_ORDER_TYPE_BUY = 0   AH_ORDER_TYPE_SELL = 1
AH_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_LIMIT = 2   AH_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_LIMIT = 3
AH_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP = 4   AH_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP = 5
AH_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP_LIMIT = 6   AH_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP_LIMIT = 7   AH_ORDER_TYPE_CLOSE_BY = 8

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError. Longer internal deadline (history can be large).
  • The ticket accessor is position_ticket, not ticket.
  • Filters by open time — a position opened before from_utc but closed inside the window is not included.
  • One row per round-trip — simpler than order_history for performance stats.

docs.title: 1) Last 7 days of closed positions
docs.text:
from = Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600
acct.positions_history(from_utc: from).each do |p|
  puts format("#%d  %-8s  vol %.2f  %s → %s  profit %.2f",
              p.position_ticket, p.symbol, p.volume, p.open_price, p.close_price, p.profit)
end

docs.title: 2) Win rate
docs.text:
rows = acct.positions_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600)
wins = rows.count { |p| p.profit.positive? }
puts "win rate: #{(100.0 * wins / rows.size).round(1)}% of #{rows.size}"

docs.title: 3) Best & worst trade
docs.text:
rows = acct.positions_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30 * 24 * 3600)
puts "best #{rows.max_by(&:profit)&.profit}  worst #{rows.min_by(&:profit)&.profit}"

docs.title: 4) Net result including costs
docs.text:
rows = acct.positions_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7 * 24 * 3600)
net = rows.sum { |p| p.profit + p.swap + p.commission + p.fee }
puts "net (incl. costs): #{net.round(2)}"

docs.title: Equity-curve points
docs.text:
def equity_curve(acct, days: 30)
  running = 0.0
  acct.positions_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - days * 24 * 3600)
      .sort_by { |p| p.close_time.seconds }
      .map { |p| running += p.profit; [p.close_time.seconds, running.round(2)] }
end

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• OrderHistory — orders + deals (finer grain).
  • Friendly layer: MT5Sugar#positions_history · MT5Service#positions_history.

docs.title: 🔢 Counting Open Positions
docs.text:
Request: the number of open positions (PositionsTotalData) — the cheapest "are we in the market?" probe.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#positions_total (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Proto definition: PositionsTotal (defined in mt5-term-api-trade-functions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Method: PositionsTotal(google.protobuf.Empty) → PositionsTotalReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::TradeFunctions::Stub#positions_total(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One tiny RPC returning how many positions are currently open.
  • Why you need it. Gate new entries ("max N concurrent"), detect a flat account, or drive a "wait until closed" loop — without pulling the full book.
  • Sanity check. 0 on a flat account; grows by one per order_send market fill.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
positions_total is the lightest open-state read. When you only need the count (not the details), it beats opened_orders: no list to transfer, no fields to parse.

Need the tickets but still cheap? opened_orders_tickets. Need full detail? opened_orders.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def positions_total -> Integer
end

Request message: google.protobuf.Empty (no fields). Reply: the SDK returns data.total_positions (an Integer).

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: None.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: An Integer — the count of open positions.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError on failure; wrap in begin/rescue.
  • Positions, not orders. This counts filled positions, not pending orders — those live in opened_orders.opened_orders.
  • Cheap to poll, but for a push signal on changes use on_trade.

docs.title: 1) Quick count
docs.text: puts "open positions: #{acct.positions_total}"

docs.title: 2) Gate new entries
docs.text:
MAX = 5
return if acct.positions_total >= MAX   # refuse to over-trade

docs.title: 3) Flat check
docs.text: puts acct.positions_total.zero? ? "flat" : "in market"

docs.title: 4) Wait until the account is flat
docs.text:
sleep 1 until acct.positions_total.zero?
puts "all closed"

docs.title: Concurrency guard
docs.text:
def can_open?(acct, max: 5)
  acct.positions_total < max
rescue MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError
  false
end

docs.title: 💰 Calculating Required Margin
docs.text:
Request: the margin needed to open an order (OrderCalcMarginData) — before you send it.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#order_calc_margin(symbol:, type:, volume:, price:) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Proto definition: OrderCalcMargin (defined in mt5-term-api-trade-functions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Method: OrderCalcMargin(OrderCalcMarginRequest) → OrderCalcMarginReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::TradeFunctions::Stub#order_calc_margin(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning the margin (account currency) to open volume lots of symbol at price.
  • Why you need it. Size positions to your free margin, and reject trades you can't afford before sending them.
  • Sanity check. Margin for 0.1 lot EURUSD ≈ contract × price × 0.1 / leverage.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: order_calc_margin turns a trade idea into a cash requirement. Compare it to account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE) to answer "does this fit?", or invert it to find the largest affordable volume.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # type: :buy / :sell / :buy_limit / ... (mapped to ORDER_TYPE_TF_*).
  def order_calc_margin(symbol:, type:, volume:, price:) -> Float
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String (keyword) Symbol. type Symbol (keyword) :buy / :sell / :buy_limit / … volume Float (keyword) Lots. price Float (keyword) Price to calculate at (e.g. current ask).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: A Float — the margin in the account currency.

docs.title: type → ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF
docs.text:
The method maps a friendly symbol — or pass the raw ORDER_TYPE_TF_* symbol directly:

Friendly type: Raw enum # :buy ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY 0 :sell ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL 1 :buy_limit ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY_LIMIT 2 :sell_limit ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL_LIMIT 3 :buy_stop ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY_STOP 4 :sell_stop ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL_STOP 5 — (raw only) ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY_STOP_LIMIT 6 — (raw only) ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL_STOP_LIMIT 7 — (raw only) ORDER_TYPE_TF_CLOSE_BY 8

For margin, :buy and :sell give the same figure; direction only matters for the pending variants.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • Buy vs sell can differ on some instruments — pass the real direction.
  • Leverage-sensitive: the same volume costs less margin at higher leverage.

docs.title: 1) Margin for a planned trade
docs.text:
ask = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD").ask
puts acct.order_calc_margin(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, price: ask).round(2)

docs.title: 2) Does it fit free margin?
docs.text:
need = acct.order_calc_margin(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 1.0, price: ask)
free = acct.account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE)
puts need <= free ? "affordable" : "too big (#{need.round(2)} > #{free.round(2)})"

docs.title: 3) Largest affordable volume (rounded to step)
docs.text:
per_lot = acct.order_calc_margin(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 1.0, price: ask)
step    = acct.symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP)
free    = acct.account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE)
max_lot = ((free / per_lot) / step).floor * step
puts "max lot: #{max_lot}"

docs.title: 4) Compare buy vs sell
docs.text: %i[buy sell].each { |t| puts "#{t}: #{acct.order_calc_margin(symbol: 'EURUSD', type: t, volume: 0.1, price: ask).round(2)}" }

docs.title: Affordability guard
docs.text:
def affordable?(acct, sym, vol, type: :buy)
  price = acct.symbol_info_tick(sym).ask
  acct.order_calc_margin(symbol: sym, type: type, volume: vol, price: price) <=
    acct.account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE)
end

docs.title: 📈 Calculating Profit of a Move
docs.text:
Request: the profit of a hypothetical round-trip (OrderCalcProfitData) — open at one price, close at another — without trading.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#order_calc_profit(symbol:, type:, volume:, open_price:, close_price:) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Proto definition: OrderCalcProfit (defined in mt5-term-api-trade-functions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Method: OrderCalcProfit(OrderCalcProfitRequest) → OrderCalcProfitReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::TradeFunctions::Stub#order_calc_profit(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning the profit (account currency) if volume lots of symbol move from open_price to close_price.
  • Why you need it. Price a stop-loss or take-profit in money terms, size to a fixed risk, or compute a trade's risk/reward.
  • Sanity check. A :buy with close_price > open_price returns a positive number.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: order_calc_profit turns a price move into money — the complement of order_calc_margin. Use it to translate a stop distance into risk, a target into reward, and to size a position so a stop costs a fixed amount.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # type: :buy / :sell / ... (mapped to ORDER_TYPE_TF_*).
  def order_calc_profit(symbol:, type:, volume:, open_price:, close_price:) -> Float
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String (keyword) Symbol. type Symbol (keyword) :buy / :sell / … volume Float (keyword) Lots. open_price Float (keyword) Hypothetical entry price. close_price Float (keyword) Hypothetical exit price.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: A Float — the profit in the account currency (negative = loss).

docs.title: type → ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF
docs.text:
The method maps a friendly symbol — or pass the raw ORDER_TYPE_TF_* symbol directly:

Friendly type: Raw enum # :buy ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY 0 :sell ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL 1 :buy_limit ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY_LIMIT 2 :sell_limit ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL_LIMIT 3 :buy_stop ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY_STOP 4 :sell_stop ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL_STOP 5 — (raw only) ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY_STOP_LIMIT 6 — (raw only) ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL_STOP_LIMIT 7 — (raw only) ORDER_TYPE_TF_CLOSE_BY 8

Direction matters here: :buy vs :sell flips the sign of the move between open_price and close_price.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • Direction matters: for a :sell, profit is positive when close_price < open_price.
  • Currency conversion is included — if the profit currency isn't the account currency, the result is already converted.

docs.title: 1) +100 points on 0.1 lot
docs.text:
ask = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD").ask
pt  = acct.symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_POINT)
puts acct.order_calc_profit(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1,
                            open_price: ask, close_price: ask + 100 * pt).round(2)

docs.title: 2) Value of a stop-loss (risk)
docs.text:
risk = acct.order_calc_profit(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1,
                              open_price: 1.1000, close_price: 1.0950)
puts "risk: #{risk.round(2)}"   # negative

docs.title: 3) Risk/reward of an SL/TP pair
docs.text:
r = acct.order_calc_profit(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, open_price: 1.10, close_price: 1.095)
w = acct.order_calc_profit(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, open_price: 1.10, close_price: 1.115)
puts "R:R = 1:#{(w / -r).round(2)}"

docs.title: 4) Size to a fixed dollar risk
docs.text:
per_01 = -acct.order_calc_profit(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, open_price: 1.10, close_price: 1.095)
target_risk = 50.0
vol = (0.1 * target_risk / per_01).round(2)
puts "volume for $#{target_risk} risk: #{vol}"

docs.title: Fixed-risk position sizing
docs.text:
def size_for_risk(acct, sym, entry, stop, risk_money, type: :buy)
  loss_01 = -acct.order_calc_profit(symbol: sym, type: type, volume: 0.1, open_price: entry, close_price: stop)
  step    = acct.symbol_info_double(sym, :SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP)
  raw     = 0.1 * risk_money / loss_01
  (raw / step).floor * step
end
