docs.title: 🧪 Validating a Trade Request
docs.text:
Request: check whether a trade request would succeed — margin, free margin, retcode — without sending it (OrderCheckData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#order_check(request) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Proto definition: OrderCheck (defined in mt5-term-api-trade-functions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • Method: OrderCheck(OrderCheckRequest) → OrderCheckReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::TradeFunctions::Stub#order_check(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A dry-run: the server validates a trade request and returns the would-be margin / free margin / retcode — but places nothing.
  • Why you need it. Confirm affordability and a clean retcode before committing with order_send.
  • Sanity check. A valid 0.1-lot request on a funded demo returns a result with a success retcode.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: order_check is the "would this go through?" gate. It's the safe way to test sizing and stops against the account's margin without touching the market — ideal before an automated entry.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # `request` is a Mt5TermApi::MrpcMqlTradeRequest.
  def order_check(request) -> Mt5TermApi::OrderCheckData
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text:
Parameter Type Description request MrpcMqlTradeRequest The trade to validate. Key fields: symbol, volume, order_type (an ORDER_TYPE_TF_* enum), price. 
req = Mt5TermApi::MrpcMqlTradeRequest.new(
  symbol: "EURUSD", volume: 0.1, order_type: :ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY,
  price: acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD").ask
)

⚠️ Enum gotcha: order_type here uses the trade-functions enum ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY (not the trading-helper TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY). See SymbolInfoMarginRate for the third order-type enum.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCheckData
docs.text: • mql_trade_check_result — the check result message: retcode, balance/equity/margin after the hypothetical trade, free margin, margin level, comment.

docs.title: 🧱 Enum values (raw — you build the MrpcMqlTradeRequest)
docs.text: order_check takes a pre-built request, so set these fields with the raw enum symbols:

docs.title: action → MRPC_ENUM_TRADE_REQUEST_ACTIONS
docs.text:
TRADE_ACTION_DEAL     = 0   // market deal
TRADE_ACTION_PENDING  = 1   // place a pending order
TRADE_ACTION_SLTP     = 2   // modify SL/TP of a position
TRADE_ACTION_MODIFY   = 3   // modify a pending order
TRADE_ACTION_REMOVE   = 4   // delete a pending order
TRADE_ACTION_CLOSE_BY = 5   // close by an opposite position

docs.title: order_type → ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF
docs.text:
ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY = 0   ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL = 1
ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY_LIMIT = 2   ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL_LIMIT = 3
ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY_STOP = 4   ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL_STOP = 5
ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY_STOP_LIMIT = 6   ORDER_TYPE_TF_SELL_STOP_LIMIT = 7   ORDER_TYPE_TF_CLOSE_BY = 8

docs.title: type_filling → MRPC_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_FILLING
docs.text: ORDER_FILLING_FOK = 0   ORDER_FILLING_IOC = 1   ORDER_FILLING_RETURN = 2   ORDER_FILLING_BOC = 3

docs.title: type_time → MRPC_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TIME
docs.text: ORDER_TIME_GTC = 0   ORDER_TIME_DAY = 1   ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED = 2   ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED_DAY = 3

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure. (It never places a trade.)
  • Build the request once, reuse it for several sizes by changing volume.
  • Pre-flight, not a guarantee — the market can move between order_check and order_send; keep stops sane.

docs.title: 1) Validate before sending
docs.text:
req = Mt5TermApi::MrpcMqlTradeRequest.new(symbol: "EURUSD", volume: 0.1,
        order_type: :ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY, price: acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD").ask)
res = acct.order_check(req)
puts res.mql_trade_check_result ? "ok to send" : "check failed"

docs.title: 2) Affordability gate before order_send
docs.text:
if acct.order_check(req).mql_trade_check_result
  acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1)
else
  warn "not affordable / rejected"
end

docs.title: 3) Find the biggest volume that passes
docs.text:
ask = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD").ask
vol = [5.0, 1.0, 0.1].find do |v|
  r = Mt5TermApi::MrpcMqlTradeRequest.new(symbol: "EURUSD", volume: v, order_type: :ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY, price: ask)
  acct.order_check(r).mql_trade_check_result
end
puts "largest ok: #{vol}"

docs.title: Reusable checker
docs.text:
def affordable?(acct, symbol, volume)
  ask = acct.symbol_info_tick(symbol).ask
  req = Mt5TermApi::MrpcMqlTradeRequest.new(symbol: symbol, volume: volume, order_type: :ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY, price: ask)
  !acct.order_check(req).mql_trade_check_result.nil?
rescue MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError
  false
end

docs.text:
• OrderCalcMargin · OrderCalcProfit · OrderSend
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service#order_check.

docs.title: ❌ Closing an Order
docs.text:
Request: close a position (fully or partially) or delete a pending order (OrderCloseData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#order_close(ticket:, volume:, slippage:) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderClose (defined in mt5-term-api-trading-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Method: OrderClose(OrderCloseRequest) → OrderCloseReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::TradingHelper::Stub#order_close(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One trade RPC that exits a position — full or partial — or deletes a pending order, by ticket.
  • Why you need it. Take profit / cut a loss, scale out of a position, or cancel a working order.
  • Sanity check. Success ⇒ returned_code == 10009; close_mode says whether it was a close or a delete.

⚠️ Exactly-once. Sent once, never re-sent. On a transport failure re-read the position before retrying.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: order_close is your exit. On a position ticket it closes (all or part of the volume); on a pending ticket it deletes the order. One method covers both — close_mode in the reply tells you which happened.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # Close a position (volume nil/0 = full) or delete a pending order by ticket.
  def order_close(ticket:, volume: nil, slippage: 10) -> Mt5TermApi::OrderCloseData
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description ticket Integer (required) Position or pending-order ticket. volume Float Lots to close; nil/0 = full close. slippage Integer (default 10) Max price deviation (points).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCloseData
docs.text: Field Ruby accessor Type Description returned_code returned_code Integer 10009 = DONE. returned_string_code returned_string_code String Retcode as text. returned_code_description returned_code_description String Human-readable description. close_mode close_mode Symbol How it was closed (close / delete) enum.

docs.title: close_mode (output) → MRPC_ORDER_CLOSE_MODE
docs.text:
What the server did, returned on OrderCloseData.close_mode:

MRPC_MARKET_ORDER_CLOSE         = 0   // a market position fully closed
MRPC_MARKET_ORDER_PARTIAL_CLOSE = 1   // a market position partially closed
MRPC_PENDING_ORDER_REMOVE       = 2   // a pending order deleted

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: a rejection raises ApiError; a transport failure may raise a TradeOutcomeUnknown-marked error.
  • Partial close: pass a volume smaller than the position; the remainder stays open as a new/continuing position.
  • Pending orders: order_close on a pending ticket deletes it (no fill).
  • Slippage guards against adverse moves on a market close — widen it on fast markets.

docs.title: 1) Full close
docs.text:
out = acct.order_close(ticket: 123_456)
puts out.returned_code == 10_009 ? "closed" : out.returned_code_description

docs.title: 2) Partial close (half)
docs.text: acct.order_close(ticket: 123_456, volume: 0.05)

docs.title: 3) Delete a pending order
docs.text: acct.order_close(ticket: pending_ticket)   # pending → deleted

docs.title: 4) Close everything on a symbol
docs.text:
acct.opened_orders.position_infos
    .select { |p| p.symbol == "EURUSD" }
    .each   { |p| acct.order_close(ticket: p.ticket) }

docs.title: Close-all with a result summary
docs.text:
def close_all(acct)
  acct.opened_orders.position_infos.map do |p|
    r = acct.order_close(ticket: p.ticket)
    [p.ticket, r.returned_code]
  end.to_h
end

docs.title: ✏️ Modifying an Order
docs.text:
Request: change SL/TP of a position, or price/SL/TP/expiration of a pending order (OrderModifyData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#order_modify(ticket:, ...) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Proto definition: OrderModify (defined in mt5-term-api-trading-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.TradingHelper
  • Method: OrderModify(OrderModifyRequest) → OrderModifyReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::TradingHelper::Stub#order_modify(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One trade RPC that edits an existing ticket — attach/move SL & TP on a position, or retune a pending order's price and expiry.
  • Why you need it. Trail a stop, lock in profit, re-price a pending order as the market moves.
  • Sanity check. Success ⇒ returned_code == 10009.

⚠️ Exactly-once. Like every trade call, this is sent once and never re-sent. A transport failure after the request may have reached the terminal is marked TradeOutcomeUnknown — re-read the position before retrying.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: order_modify is position/order maintenance. The common job is moving a stop-loss (manual lock-in or an automated trailing stop); the other is re-pricing a working pending order. It never changes volume — for that, close and re-open.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def order_modify(ticket:, stop_loss: nil, take_profit: nil, price: nil,
                   stop_limit: nil, expiration_type: nil, expiration_utc: nil) -> Mt5TermApi::OrderModifyData
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description ticket Integer (required) Position or order ticket. stop_loss / take_profit Float New protective prices. price Float New price (pending orders). stop_limit Float New stop-limit trigger. expiration_type / expiration_utc enum / Time New expiry (pending orders).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderModifyData
docs.text: Same shape as OrderSendData: returned_code (10009 = DONE), order, returned_string_code, returned_code_description, …

docs.title: expiration_type → TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TIME (raw symbol — passed through, no friendly alias)
docs.text:
TMT5_ORDER_TIME_GTC           = 0
TMT5_ORDER_TIME_DAY           = 1
TMT5_ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED     = 2
TMT5_ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED_DAY = 3

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: a rejection raises ApiError; a transport failure may raise a TradeOutcomeUnknown-marked error.
  • Respect the min stop distance (:SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL) — SL/TP too close to price are rejected.
  • Round new prices to the symbol's digits (:SYMBOL_DIGITS).
  • Only moves what you pass — omit take_profit: and the existing TP is left untouched.

docs.title: 1) Attach / move a stop-loss
docs.text:
pt  = acct.symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_POINT)
d   = acct.symbol_info_integer("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_DIGITS)
bid = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD").bid
acct.order_modify(ticket: 123_456, stop_loss: (bid - 200 * pt).round(d))

docs.title: 2) Set both SL and TP
docs.text: acct.order_modify(ticket: 123_456, stop_loss: 1.0800, take_profit: 1.1000)

docs.title: 3) Re-price a pending order
docs.text: acct.order_modify(ticket: 123_456, price: 1.0750)

docs.title: 4) One trailing-stop step (ratchet up only)
docs.text:
pt = acct.symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_POINT)
d  = acct.symbol_info_integer("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_DIGITS)
want = (acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD").bid - 150 * pt).round(d)
acct.order_modify(ticket: 123_456, stop_loss: want) if want > @best_sl.to_f
@best_sl = want

docs.title: Safe-modify respecting the stops level
docs.text:
def safe_sl(acct, sym, ticket, sl)
  pt    = acct.symbol_info_double(sym, :SYMBOL_POINT)
  d     = acct.symbol_info_integer(sym, :SYMBOL_DIGITS)
  stops = acct.symbol_info_integer(sym, :SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL)
  bid   = acct.symbol_info_tick(sym).bid
  sl    = [sl, bid - stops * pt].min            # keep it outside the stops level
  acct.order_modify(ticket: ticket, stop_loss: sl.round(d))
end

docs.title: 🚀 Sending an Order
docs.text:
Request: open a market or pending order (OrderSendData). The core trade call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#order_send(symbol:, type:, volume:, ...) · gRPC: mt5_term_api.TradingHelper · Proto: OrderSend

docs.title: RPC
docs.text: OrderSend(OrderSendRequest) → OrderSendReply — the SDK returns data (OrderSendData).

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Opens a position (market) or places a pending order.
  • Why you need it. It's how you enter the market.
  • Sanity check. Success ⇒ returned_code == 10009 (TRADE_RETCODE_DONE); order / deal are non-zero.

⚠️ Exactly-once. A trade is sent once and never re-sent by the SDK. A transport failure may leave the outcome unknown (TradeOutcomeUnknown) — check positions/history before retrying.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def order_send(symbol:, type:, volume:,
                 price: nil, stop_loss: nil, take_profit: nil, comment: nil,
                 magic: nil, slippage: nil, stop_limit_price: nil,
                 expiration_type: nil, expiration_utc: nil, quotes_wait_ms: nil,
                 without_checks: false) -> Mt5TermApi::OrderSendData
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String (required) Symbol, e.g. "EURUSD". type Symbol (required) :buy / :sell / :buy_limit / :sell_limit / :buy_stop / :sell_stop / :buy_stop_limit / :sell_stop_limit. volume Float (required) Lots. price Float Entry price. Required for pending orders; for market orders the server fills at market. stop_loss / take_profit Float Protective prices (optional). comment String Free-text tag (optional). magic Integer EA magic → expert_id (optional). slippage Integer Max price deviation (optional). stop_limit_price Float Trigger price for stop-limit orders. expiration_type / expiration_utc enum / Time Pending-order expiry (optional). without_checks Boolean Use OrderSendWithoutChecks (skip terminal-side checks).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderSendData
docs.text: Field Ruby accessor Type Description returned_code returned_code Integer Trade-server retcode — 10009 = DONE. order order Integer New order ticket. deal deal Integer Resulting deal ticket (market orders). volume volume Float Filled volume. price price Float Fill price. bid / ask bid / ask Float Market at execution. comment comment String Server comment. returned_string_code returned_string_code String Retcode as text. returned_code_description returned_code_description String Human-readable description.

docs.title: type → TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE
docs.text:
The method maps a friendly symbol to the wire enum — or pass the raw TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_* symbol directly:

Friendly type: Raw enum # :buy TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY 0 :sell TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL 1 :buy_limit TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_LIMIT 2 :sell_limit TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_LIMIT 3 :buy_stop TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP 4 :sell_stop TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP 5 :buy_stop_limit TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP_LIMIT 6 :sell_stop_limit TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP_LIMIT 7 — (raw only) TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_CLOSE_BY 8

docs.title: expiration_type → TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TIME (raw symbol — no friendly alias)
docs.text:
TMT5_ORDER_TIME_GTC           = 0
TMT5_ORDER_TIME_DAY           = 1
TMT5_ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED     = 2
TMT5_ORDER_TIME_SPECIFIED_DAY = 3

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: a rejection raises ApiError; a transport failure may raise a TradeOutcomeUnknown-marked error — do not blindly retry.
  • Round prices to the symbol's digits (symbol_info_integer(sym, :SYMBOL_DIGITS)) and respect the min stop distance (:SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL).
  • Market vs pending: pending orders require price: (and face/break the market per type).

docs.title: 1) Market buy
docs.text:
r = acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, magic: 600001, comment: "entry")
if r.returned_code == 10_009
  puts "opened order ##{r.order} deal ##{r.deal} @ #{r.price}"
else
  puts "rejected: #{r.returned_code} #{r.returned_code_description}"
end

docs.title: 2) Market buy with SL/TP
docs.text:
t = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD"); d = acct.symbol_info_integer("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_DIGITS)
pt = acct.symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_POINT)
acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1,
                stop_loss: (t.bid - 500*pt).round(d), take_profit: (t.ask + 500*pt).round(d))

docs.title: 3) Pending buy-limit below market
docs.text:
bid = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD").bid
acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy_limit, volume: 0.1, price: (bid - 0.0030).round(5))

docs.text:

  • OrderCalcMargin — size before sending.
  • Friendly layer: MT5Sugar#buy_market / #buy_limit / #buy_market_with_sl_tp.

docs.title: MT5Account · Trading Operations — Overview
docs.text: Place, modify and close orders, plus the pre-trade calculators. All trade calls go through mt5_term_api.TradingHelper; the calculators/validation through TradeFunctions.

docs.title: ⚠️ Exactly-once trade safety
docs.text: Trade calls (order_send / order_modify / order_close) are sent exactly once and never re-sent by the SDK. If a trade call fails at the transport level after the request may already have reached the terminal, the error is marked TradeOutcomeUnknown — the trade may or may not have executed. Check open positions / history before retrying. See Return Codes.

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text: Method What it does OrderSend open a market or pending order OrderModify change SL/TP/price/expiration OrderClose close a position or delete a pending order OrderCheck validate a trade request without sending it OrderCalcMargin margin required for an order OrderCalcProfit profit of a hypothetical round-trip

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• Trade: order_send opens, order_modify adjusts, order_close exits. Each returns a *Data with a returned_code — 10009 = DONE.
  • Think first: order_check validates (margin / retcode) without touching the market; order_calc_margin / order_calc_profit do the pre-trade math.

Rule of thumb: size/validate with the calculators → execute with order_send → manage with order_modify / order_close.

docs.title: Quick choose
docs.text: If you need… Use Returns Open market / pending order order_send OrderSendData Change SL / TP / price order_modify OrderModifyData Close position / delete pending order_close OrderCloseData Validate before sending order_check OrderCheckData Margin for an order order_calc_margin Float Profit of a move order_calc_profit Float

docs.title: 🧱 Order-type symbols
docs.text:
order_send takes a friendly type: symbol mapped to the trading-helper enum:

type: Meaning :buy / :sell market order :buy_limit / :sell_limit pending limit (faces the market) :buy_stop / :sell_stop pending stop (breakout) :buy_stop_limit / :sell_stop_limit stop-limit

The calculators (order_calc_margin / order_calc_profit) and order_check use the trade-functions enum (ORDER_TYPE_TF_*); the SDK maps the same friendly symbols for you.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippets
docs.text:
ask = acct.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD").ask
margin = acct.order_calc_margin(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, price: ask)
puts "margin #{margin.round(2)}"

r = acct.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, magic: 600001)
puts "retcode #{r.returned_code} order ##{r.order}" if r.returned_code == 10_009

acct.order_close(ticket: r.order)

docs.title: ➕ Subscribe to the Order Book
docs.text:
Request: subscribe the terminal to a symbol's Depth of Market (MarketBookAddData). Required before market_book_get.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#market_book_add(symbol) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: MarketBookAdd (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: MarketBookAdd(MarketBookAddRequest) → MarketBookAddReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#market_book_add(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Opens a Depth-of-Market (Level-II) subscription for one symbol.
  • Why you need it. The terminal only keeps the order book for symbols you've subscribed — do this before market_book_get.
  • Sanity check. Returns true when the book opened. Many FX feeds return true but an empty ladder.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: market_book_add is step 1 of the DOM lifecycle add → get → release. It tells the gateway to start maintaining the order book for a symbol so later market_book_get snapshots have data.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def market_book_add(symbol) -> Boolean   # true if the book was opened
end

Request message: MarketBookAddRequest { string symbol = 1; } Reply: the SDK returns data.opened_successfully (a Boolean).

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String The symbol to subscribe.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: true when the subscription opened (the symbol has a book).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • Always pair with market_book_release — leaving subscriptions open wastes gateway resources.
  • Empty books are normal on retail FX — check market_book_get(...).mql_book_infos for content.
  • Select first if needed: some symbols require symbol_select before a book is available.

docs.title: 1) Guard the lifecycle
docs.text:
if acct.market_book_add("EURUSD")
  # ... read with market_book_get ...
  acct.market_book_release("EURUSD")
else
  puts "no DOM for EURUSD"
end

docs.title: 2) Subscribe a basket
docs.text: %w[EURUSD GBPUSD].each { |s| acct.market_book_add(s) }

docs.title: 3) Add, confirm it has depth, else release
docs.text:
if acct.market_book_add("XAUUSD")
  depth = acct.market_book_get("XAUUSD").mql_book_infos.size
  acct.market_book_release("XAUUSD") if depth.zero?
  puts "levels: #{depth}"
end

docs.title: With-book block (auto-release)
docs.text:
def with_book(acct, sym)
  return yield(nil) unless acct.market_book_add(sym)
  yield acct.market_book_get(sym)
ensure
  acct.market_book_release(sym)
end

docs.text:
• MarketBookGet · MarketBookRelease
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service#book_add.

docs.title: 📖 Reading the Order Book
docs.text:
Request: the current Depth-of-Market snapshot for a symbol (MarketBookGetData). Call market_book_add first.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#market_book_get(symbol) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: MarketBookGet (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: MarketBookGet(MarketBookGetRequest) → MarketBookGetReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#market_book_get(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning the current order-book ladder for a subscribed symbol.
  • Why you need it. Read Level-II liquidity — the price/volume at each bid and ask level — for microstructure, slippage estimates, or a DOM widget.
  • Sanity check. After market_book_add, mql_book_infos has levels on instruments that expose depth (often empty on retail FX).

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: market_book_get is step 2 of add → get → release: the snapshot read. It's a point-in-time picture (not a stream) — poll it, or read once per decision.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def market_book_get(symbol) -> Mt5TermApi::MarketBookGetData
end

Request message: MarketBookGetRequest { string symbol = 1; } Reply: the SDK returns data (MarketBookGetData).

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String A symbol you've subscribed with market_book_add.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — MarketBookGetData
docs.text:
• mql_book_infos → [MrpcMqlBookInfo] — the ladder. Each level:
Field Ruby accessor Type Description type type Symbol Level type (buy / sell / market buy / sell) enum. price price Float Price at this level. volume volume Integer Volume at this level. volume_real volume_real Float Real volume (where provided).

docs.title: type (output) → BookType
docs.text:
Each DOM entry's side, on MrpcBookInfo.type:

BOOK_TYPE_SELL        = 0   // ask side (resting sell)
BOOK_TYPE_BUY         = 1   // bid side (resting buy)
BOOK_TYPE_SELL_MARKET = 2   // sell at market
BOOK_TYPE_BUY_MARKET  = 3   // buy at market

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • Empty is valid — guard with .any? before indexing.
  • Snapshot, not a stream — re-call it to refresh; there's no DOM callback.
  • Subscribe first — without market_book_add the book is empty.

docs.title: 1) Count levels
docs.text:
acct.market_book_add("EURUSD")
puts acct.market_book_get("EURUSD").mql_book_infos.size
acct.market_book_release("EURUSD")

docs.title: 2) Top 5 levels
docs.text:
acct.market_book_get("EURUSD").mql_book_infos.first(5).each do |l|
  puts "#{l.type}  #{l.price} x #{l.volume}"
end

docs.title: 3) Best bid / best ask from the ladder
docs.text:
levels = acct.market_book_get("EURUSD").mql_book_infos
bids = levels.select { |l| l.type.to_s.include?("BUY") }
asks = levels.select { |l| l.type.to_s.include?("SELL") }
puts "best bid #{bids.map(&:price).max}  best ask #{asks.map(&:price).min}" if levels.any?

docs.title: Total depth on each side
docs.text:
def depth_totals(acct, sym)
  levels = acct.market_book_get(sym).mql_book_infos
  levels.group_by { |l| l.type }.transform_values { |ls| ls.sum(&:volume) }
end

docs.text:
• MarketBookAdd · MarketBookRelease
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service#book.

docs.title: ➖ Unsubscribe from the Order Book
docs.text:
Request: stop receiving a symbol's Depth of Market (MarketBookReleaseData). The clean-up step of the DOM lifecycle.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#market_book_release(symbol) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: MarketBookRelease (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: MarketBookRelease(MarketBookReleaseRequest) → MarketBookReleaseReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#market_book_release(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Closes the Depth-of-Market subscription for one symbol.
  • Why you need it. Free gateway resources when you're done reading the book — always release what you added.
  • Sanity check. Returns true when the subscription closed.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: market_book_release is step 3 of add → get → release. Leaving DOM subscriptions open keeps the gateway maintaining books you no longer read — release them as soon as you're finished.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def market_book_release(symbol) -> Boolean   # true if the book was closed
end

Request message: MarketBookReleaseRequest { string symbol = 1; } Reply: the SDK returns data.closed_successfully (a Boolean).

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String The symbol to unsubscribe.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output
docs.text: true when the subscription closed.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • Pair every add with a release — ideally in an ensure block so it runs even on error.
  • Idempotent-ish: releasing a symbol you didn't add is harmless (returns a falsey/true result depending on the gateway).

docs.title: 1) Release one
docs.text: acct.market_book_release("EURUSD")

docs.title: 2) Full add → read → release
docs.text:
if acct.market_book_add("EURUSD")
  puts acct.market_book_get("EURUSD").mql_book_infos.size
  acct.market_book_release("EURUSD")
end

docs.title: 3) Release everything you added
docs.text: %w[EURUSD GBPUSD].each { |s| acct.market_book_release(s) }

docs.title: Guaranteed release with ensure
docs.text:
acct.market_book_add("EURUSD")
begin
  book = acct.market_book_get("EURUSD").mql_book_infos
  # ... use book ...
ensure
  acct.market_book_release("EURUSD")
end

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• MarketBookAdd · MarketBookGet
  • Friendly layer: MT5Service#book_release.

Back to: Market Depth — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: MT5Account · Market Depth (DOM) — Overview
docs.text:
Level-II quotes / the order book. The lifecycle is always add → get → release: subscribe the terminal to a symbol's book, read snapshots, then unsubscribe.

All three live on mt5_term_api.MarketInfo. Not every symbol exposes a book (many FX feeds return an empty one).

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text: Method What it does MarketBookAdd subscribe to a symbol's order book MarketBookGet read the current book snapshot MarketBookRelease unsubscribe

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
1. market_book_add(sym) → start receiving depth for sym (returns true on success).
  2. market_book_get(sym) → read the current ladder (mql_book_infos).
  3. market_book_release(sym) → stop when done.

Rule of thumb: always release what you add — leaving subscriptions open wastes gateway resources.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippet
docs.text:
if acct.market_book_add("EURUSD")
  book = acct.market_book_get("EURUSD").mql_book_infos
  book.first(5).each { |lvl| puts "#{lvl.type} #{lvl.price} x #{lvl.volume}" }
  acct.market_book_release("EURUSD")
else
  puts "no DOM for EURUSD"
end

docs.text:

  • Friendly layer: MT5Sugar#book_add / #book / #book_release.

docs.title: MT5Account · Additional Methods — Overview
docs.text:
Batch symbol specs, tick value for sizing, margin rates and trading sessions. These round out the symbol/market reads that don't fit the basic Symbol-Information group.

Mixed services: symbol_params_many / tick_value_with_size on AccountHelper; symbol_info_margin_rate / symbol_info_session_quote / symbol_info_session_trade on MarketInfo.

docs.text: Method What it does SymbolParamsMany full contract spec of every symbol in one call TickValueWithSize tick value / size / contract size for sizing SymbolInfoMarginRate initial / maintenance margin rates for an order type SymbolInfoSessionQuote quote session [from, to) for a weekday SymbolInfoSessionTrade trade session [from, to) for a weekday

docs.text:
• symbol_params_many → the heavy one: one call returns the full SymbolParameters for all symbols (digits, point, lot limits, swaps, margins, currencies…). Cache it.
  • tick_value_with_size → the numbers you need to size a position (tick value / tick size / contract size).
  • symbol_info_margin_rate → margin multipliers per order type.
  • session_quote / session_trade → when a symbol quotes / trades on a given weekday.

spec = acct.symbol_params_many.find { |s| s.name == "EURUSD" }
puts "digits #{spec.digits}  min #{spec.volume_min}  step #{spec.volume_step}"

mr = acct.symbol_info_margin_rate("EURUSD", :buy)
puts "initial #{mr.initial_margin_rate}  maintenance #{mr.maintenance_margin_rate}"

docs.title: 💱 Margin Rates for an Order Type
docs.text:
Request: the initial and maintenance margin rates for a symbol at a given order type (SymbolInfoMarginRateData).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbol_info_margin_rate(symbol, order_type) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoMarginRate (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoMarginRate(SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest) → SymbolInfoMarginRateReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbol_info_margin_rate(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning the margin multipliers (initial / maintenance) the broker applies to a symbol for a given order type.
  • Why you need it. Explain why margin differs between order types, or feed a custom margin model.
  • Sanity check. initial_margin_rate is typically 1.0 for a plain market order on FX.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: symbol_info_margin_rate exposes the per-order-type margin rates behind order_calc_margin. Pending/limit/stop types can carry different rates than market orders — read them when you need the exact multiplier rather than the final figure.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # order_type: :buy / :sell / :buy_limit / ... (mapped to the MQL ORDER_TYPE_* enum),
  # or a raw :ORDER_TYPE_* symbol.
  def symbol_info_margin_rate(symbol, order_type) -> Mt5TermApi::SymbolInfoMarginRateData
end

⚠️ Enum gotcha (third one!): this RPC uses the MQL ENUM_ORDER_TYPE (ORDER_TYPE_BUY, ORDER_TYPE_SELL, …) — not order_send's TMT5_ORDER_TYPE_* and not the calculators' ORDER_TYPE_TF_*. The SDK maps friendly :buy / :sell symbols to :ORDER_TYPE_BUY for you.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String The symbol. order_type Symbol :buy / :sell / :buy_limit / … (or a raw :ORDER_TYPE_*).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoMarginRateData
docs.text: Ruby accessor Type Description initial_margin_rate Float Initial margin multiplier. maintenance_margin_rate Float Maintenance margin multiplier.

docs.title: order_type → ENUM_ORDER_TYPE (MQL)
docs.text:
The method accepts a friendly symbol (it upcases :buy → :ORDER_TYPE_BUY) — or pass the raw ORDER_TYPE_* symbol directly:

Friendly order_type Raw enum # :buy ORDER_TYPE_BUY 0 :sell ORDER_TYPE_SELL 1 :buy_limit ORDER_TYPE_BUY_LIMIT 2 :sell_limit ORDER_TYPE_SELL_LIMIT 3 :buy_stop ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP 4 :sell_stop ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP 5 :buy_stop_limit ORDER_TYPE_BUY_STOP_LIMIT 6 :sell_stop_limit ORDER_TYPE_SELL_STOP_LIMIT 7 :close_by ORDER_TYPE_CLOSE_BY 8

This is the MQL ENUM_ORDER_TYPE (no prefix) — distinct from order_send's TMT5_ENUM_ORDER_TYPE and the calculators' ENUM_ORDER_TYPE_TF.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • Want the money figure, not the rate? Use order_calc_margin — it applies these rates for you.
  • Rates can be 0 on some instruments/types — don't divide by them blindly.

docs.title: 1) Initial / maintenance for a buy
docs.text:
mr = acct.symbol_info_margin_rate("EURUSD", :buy)
puts "initial #{mr.initial_margin_rate}  maintenance #{mr.maintenance_margin_rate}"

docs.title: 2) Compare buy vs sell
docs.text:
%i[buy sell].each do |t|
  puts "#{t}: #{acct.symbol_info_margin_rate('EURUSD', t).initial_margin_rate}"
end

docs.title: 3) Pending vs market

%i[buy buy_limit buy_stop].each do |t|

docs.title: 🕐 Quote Session Times
docs.text:
Request: the quote session [from, to) for a symbol on a given weekday (SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData) — when the symbol is quoted.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbol_info_session_quote(symbol, day_of_week:, session_index:) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoSessionQuote (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoSessionQuote(SymbolInfoSessionQuoteRequest) → SymbolInfoSessionQuoteReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbol_info_session_quote(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning a single quote-session window for a symbol on one weekday.
  • Why you need it. Know when prices are being published (vs when you can actually trade — see symbol_info_session_trade).
  • Sanity check. On a 24/5 FX major, weekdays return a long window; Saturday/Sunday are usually empty or closed.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: symbol_info_session_quote tells you the broker's quoting hours. Combined with the trade session, it lets a bot avoid acting outside market hours or during thin, quote-only windows.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # day_of_week: an ENUM_DAY_OF_WEEK symbol (:SUNDAY .. :SATURDAY).
  def symbol_info_session_quote(symbol, day_of_week:, session_index: 0) -> Mt5TermApi::SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String The symbol. day_of_week Symbol (keyword) :SUNDAY … :SATURDAY. session_index Integer (keyword, default 0) Which session on that day (0-based).

docs.title: 🧱 Day enum — DayOfWeek (all 7)
docs.text:
SUNDAY    = 0
MONDAY    = 1
TUESDAY   = 2
WEDNESDAY = 3
THURSDAY  = 4
FRIDAY    = 5
SATURDAY  = 6

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData
docs.text: Ruby accessor Type Description from message Session start (read .seconds). to message Session end (read .seconds).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • from / to are seconds-of-day style messages — read .seconds.
  • Multiple sessions: bump session_index (0, 1, 2…) to walk a day with breaks; stop when the call errors / returns empty.
  • Quote ≠ trade: quoting can be wider than the tradable window — compare with symbol_info_session_trade.

docs.title: 1) Monday quote session
docs.text:
sq = acct.symbol_info_session_quote("EURUSD", day_of_week: :MONDAY)
puts "#{sq.from&.seconds}s → #{sq.to&.seconds}s"

docs.title: 2) Whole week at a glance
docs.text:
%i[MONDAY TUESDAY WEDNESDAY THURSDAY FRIDAY].each do |d|
  s = acct.symbol_info_session_quote("EURUSD", day_of_week: d)
  puts "#{d}: #{s.from&.seconds} → #{s.to&.seconds}"
end

docs.title: 3) Walk multiple sessions of a day
docs.text:
i = 0
loop do
  s = acct.symbol_info_session_quote("XAUUSD", day_of_week: :MONDAY, session_index: i)
  break if s.from.nil?
  puts "session #{i}: #{s.from.seconds} → #{s.to.seconds}"
  i += 1
rescue MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError
  break
end

docs.title: Seconds-of-day → "HH:MM"
docs.text:
def hhmm(secs)
  format("%02d:%02d", secs / 3600, (secs % 3600) / 60)
end
sq = acct.symbol_info_session_quote("EURUSD", day_of_week: :MONDAY)
puts "#{hhmm(sq.from.seconds)}–#{hhmm(sq.to.seconds)}"

docs.title: 🕑 Trade Session Times
docs.text:
Request: the trade session [from, to) for a symbol on a given weekday (SymbolInfoSessionTradeData) — when the symbol can actually be traded.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbol_info_session_trade(symbol, day_of_week:, session_index:) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Proto definition: SymbolInfoSessionTrade (defined in mt5-term-api-market-info.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • Method: SymbolInfoSessionTrade(SymbolInfoSessionTradeRequest) → SymbolInfoSessionTradeReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::MarketInfo::Stub#symbol_info_session_trade(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning a single trade-session window for a symbol on one weekday.
  • Why you need it. Gate order placement to market hours — don't send into a closed session.
  • Sanity check. Trade windows are usually equal to or narrower than the quote windows.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: symbol_info_session_trade is the "can I trade now?" calendar. Use it to skip entries when the instrument is quote-only or closed, and to schedule activity around session opens/closes.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def symbol_info_session_trade(symbol, day_of_week:, session_index: 0) -> Mt5TermApi::SymbolInfoSessionTradeData
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbol String The symbol. day_of_week Symbol (keyword) :SUNDAY … :SATURDAY. session_index Integer (keyword, default 0) Which session on that day (0-based).

docs.title: 🧱 Day enum — DayOfWeek (all 7)
docs.text:
SUNDAY    = 0
MONDAY    = 1
TUESDAY   = 2
WEDNESDAY = 3
THURSDAY  = 4
FRIDAY    = 5
SATURDAY  = 6

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoSessionTradeData
docs.text: Ruby accessor Type Description from message Session start (read .seconds). to message Session end (read .seconds).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • Quote vs trade: a symbol may quote outside the window in which it can be traded — compare against symbol_info_session_quote.
  • Weekends are typically empty/closed on FX — handle nil from.

docs.title: 1) Monday trade session
docs.text:
st = acct.symbol_info_session_trade("EURUSD", day_of_week: :MONDAY)
puts "#{st.from&.seconds}s → #{st.to&.seconds}s"

docs.title: 2) Compare quote vs trade window
docs.text:
q = acct.symbol_info_session_quote("EURUSD", day_of_week: :MONDAY)
t = acct.symbol_info_session_trade("EURUSD", day_of_week: :MONDAY)
puts "quote #{q.from&.seconds}  ·  trade #{t.from&.seconds}"

docs.title: 3) Is a symbol tradable today?
docs.text:
day = Time.now.utc.strftime("%A").upcase.to_sym   # e.g. :MONDAY
tradable = !acct.symbol_info_session_trade("EURUSD", day_of_week: day).from.nil?
puts tradable ? "market open today" : "closed today"

docs.title: Trade-hours guard
docs.text:
def within_trade_hours?(acct, sym)
  day  = Time.now.utc.strftime("%A").upcase.to_sym
  s    = acct.symbol_info_session_trade(sym, day_of_week: day)
  return false if s.from.nil?
  now  = Time.now.utc
  secs = now.hour * 3600 + now.min * 60 + now.sec
  (s.from.seconds..s.to.seconds).cover?(secs)
end

docs.title: 📐 Full Spec of Every Symbol
docs.text:
Request: the complete contract specification of all symbols in one call ([SymbolParameters]) — digits, point, lot limits, swaps, margins, currencies and more.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#symbol_params_many(sort:) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: SymbolParamsMany (defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: SymbolParamsMany(SymbolParamsManyRequest) → SymbolParamsManyReply
  • Low-level client (generated): the SDK returns data.symbol_infos (an array of SymbolParameters).

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One (heavy) RPC returning the full spec of every symbol.
  • Why you need it. Validate/round volumes, respect the min stop distance, compute pip size, pre-trade checks — all without per-symbol round-trips.
  • Sanity check. .find { |s| s.name == "EURUSD" } returns a spec with non-zero digits / point.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
symbol_params_many is the bulk spec read — one round-trip for the whole catalog. Fetch it once at startup and cache it (index by name); every later "what's the min lot / point / stops level for X?" becomes a hash lookup instead of a network call.

Need only a few fields of one symbol? The single-property reads (symbol_info_double / integer / string) are lighter.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # Full spec of all symbols. Uses a longer internal deadline (big payload).
  def symbol_params_many(sort: nil) -> Array   # [Mt5TermApi::SymbolParameters]
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description sort Symbol (keyword, optional) Optional ordering of the result.

docs.text:

BMT5_SYMBOL_ORDERS_DAILY = 1
BMT5_SYMBOL_ORDERS_DAILY_EXCLUDING_STOPS = 2
option_mode -> BMT5_ENUM_SYMBOL_OPTION_MODE (2) 
BMT5_SYMBOL_OPTION_MODE_EUROPEAN = 0
BMT5_SYMBOL_OPTION_MODE_AMERICAN = 1
option_right -> BMT5_ENUM_SYMBOL_OPTION_RIGHT (2)

BMT5_SYMBOL_OPTION_RIGHT_PUT = 1

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError. Longer internal deadline — this is a big payload, so cache it.
  • Pip size = point × (digits == 3 || digits == 5 ? 10 : 1).
  • Round volumes to volume_step and clamp to [volume_min, volume_max] before trading.
  • Don't call it in a loop — fetch once, index by name, reuse.

docs.title: 1) One symbol's spec
docs.text:
spec = acct.symbol_params_many.find { |s| s.name == "EURUSD" }
puts "digits #{spec.digits}  point #{spec.point}  min #{spec.volume_min}  step #{spec.volume_step}"

docs.title: 2) Round a volume to the symbol's step
docs.text:
def round_volume(spec, lots)
  step = spec.volume_step.positive? ? spec.volume_step : 0.01
  v = (lots / step).round * step
  v.clamp(spec.volume_min, spec.volume_max)
end

docs.title: 3) Index the catalog once (cache)
docs.text:
SPECS = acct.symbol_params_many.to_h { |s| [s.name, s] }
puts SPECS["EURUSD"].trade_contract_size

docs.title: 4) Smallest-min-lot instruments
docs.text: acct.symbol_params_many.sort_by(&:volume_min).first(5).each { |s| puts "#{s.name} #{s.volume_min}" }

docs.title: Spec cache with lazy refresh
docs.text:
class SpecCache
  def initialize(acct) = (@acct = acct; @by_name = {})
  def [](sym)
    @by_name = @acct.symbol_params_many.to_h { |s| [s.name, s] } if @by_name.empty?
    @by_name[sym]
  end
end

docs.title: 🧮 Tick Value / Size / Contract
docs.text:
Request: tick value, tick size and contract size for one or more symbols (TickValueWithSizeData) — the numbers you need to size a position in money terms.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#tick_value_with_size(symbols) (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Proto definition: TickValueWithSize (defined in mt5-term-api-account-helper.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • Method: TickValueWithSize(TickValueWithSizeRequest) → TickValueWithSizeReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::AccountHelper::Stub#tick_value_with_size(request, metadata:, deadline:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One RPC returning the sizing triple — tick value, tick size, contract size — for one symbol or a batch.
  • Why you need it. Convert a stop distance in points into money, and a money risk into a lot size.
  • Sanity check. For EURUSD on a USD account, TradeTickValue ≈ 1.0 and TradeTickSize ≈ 1.0e-05.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
tick_value_with_size is the risk-sizing read: with tick value and tick size you know the money value of one point, and with contract size you can reason about exposure — the basis for "how many lots for $X of risk?".

⚠️ PascalCase gotcha: each TickSizeSymbol entry exposes PascalCase accessors — tv.TradeTickValue, not tv.trade_tick_value.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # `symbols` is a String or an Array of symbol names.
  def tick_value_with_size(symbols) -> Mt5TermApi::TickValueWithSizeData
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbols String or [String] One symbol or several.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — TickValueWithSizeData
docs.text:
• symbol_tick_size_infos → array of TickSizeSymbol:
Ruby accessor Type Description Name String Symbol. TradeTickValue Float Value of one tick (account currency). TradeTickValueProfit Float Tick value for a profitable position. TradeTickValueLoss Float Tick value for a losing position. TradeTickSize Float Minimal price change. TradeContractSize Float Contract size (units per lot).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Errors are exceptions: raises ApiError on failure.
  • PascalCase accessors — capital T (TradeTickValue), same style as SymbolListData.Symbols.
  • Money per point ≈ TradeTickValue × (point / TradeTickSize), where point is symbol_info_double(sym, :SYMBOL_POINT).

docs.title: 1) One symbol
docs.text:
tv = acct.tick_value_with_size("EURUSD").symbol_tick_size_infos.first
puts "tick value #{tv.TradeTickValue}  tick size #{tv.TradeTickSize}  contract #{tv.TradeContractSize}"

docs.title: 2) Several at once
docs.text:
acct.tick_value_with_size(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD XAUUSD]).symbol_tick_size_infos.each do |x|
  puts "#{x.Name}: #{x.TradeTickValue}"
end

docs.title: 3) Money value of one point
docs.text:
tv = acct.tick_value_with_size("EURUSD").symbol_tick_size_infos.first
pt = acct.symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_POINT)
puts (tv.TradeTickValue * (pt / tv.TradeTickSize)).round(4)

docs.title: Lots for a fixed point-risk
docs.text:
def lots_for_risk(acct, sym, stop_points, risk_money)
  tv   = acct.tick_value_with_size(sym).symbol_tick_size_infos.first
  pt   = acct.symbol_info_double(sym, :SYMBOL_POINT)
  per_point_per_lot = tv.TradeTickValue * (pt / tv.TradeTickSize)
  step = acct.symbol_info_double(sym, :SYMBOL_VOLUME_STEP)
  raw  = risk_money / (stop_points * per_point_per_lot)
  (raw / step).floor * step
end

docs.title: 🔔 Streaming Position P/L
docs.text:
Stream: position profit/loss updates on a timer (OnPositionProfitData) — new, updated and deleted positions since the last tick.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#on_position_profit(interval_ms:, ignore_empty:) { |data| ... } (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnPositionProfit (defined in mt5-term-api-subscriptions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnPositionProfit(OnPositionProfitRequest) → stream OnPositionProfitReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::SubscriptionService::Stub#on_position_profit(request, metadata:, return_op:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A timer-driven stream emitting your open positions' P/L every interval_ms.
  • Why you need it. A live floating-P/L readout for a dashboard, trailing logic, or a drawdown kill-switch.
  • Sanity check. With an open position, snapshots arrive ~once per interval_ms and carry updated_positions.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: on_position_profit is the live P/L feed. Unlike on_trade (which fires on changes), this fires on a timer so you always have a current profit figure — ideal for monitoring and risk guards.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def on_position_profit(interval_ms: 1000, ignore_empty: true, &block) -> MetaRPC::MT5::Subscription
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description interval_ms Integer (keyword, default 1000) How often to emit a snapshot. ignore_empty Boolean (keyword, default true) Skip empty snapshots (no positions). &block proc(data) Called per snapshot.

docs.title: ⬆️ Yielded — OnPositionProfitData
docs.text: Ruby accessor Type Description new_positions message[] Positions opened since last snapshot. updated_positions message[] Positions whose P/L changed. deleted_positions message[] Positions closed since last snapshot. account_info message Account snapshot.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Pick a sane interval_ms — 1000 is a good default; too small floods your block.
  • ignore_empty: true suppresses snapshots when you're flat — flip to false to get heartbeats anyway.
  • sub.cancel to stop; keep the block short.

docs.title: 1) Live floating P/L
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_position_profit(interval_ms: 1000) do |d|
  puts "floating: #{d.updated_positions.sum(&:profit).round(2)}"
end
sleep 5; sub.cancel

docs.title: 2) Drawdown alert
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_position_profit do |d|
  total = d.updated_positions.sum(&:profit)
  puts "⚠️ drawdown #{total.round(2)}" if total < -50
end

docs.title: 3) React to opens/closes within the feed
docs.text:
acct.on_position_profit do |d|
  d.new_positions.each     { |p| puts "opened ##{p.ticket}" }
  d.deleted_positions.each { |p| puts "closed ##{p.ticket}" }
end

docs.title: Kill-switch on floating drawdown
docs.text:
def arm_kill_switch(acct, limit:)
  acct.on_position_profit(interval_ms: 1000) do |d|
    if d.updated_positions.sum(&:profit) <= -limit
      acct.opened_orders.position_infos.each { |p| acct.order_close(ticket: p.ticket) }
    end
  end
end

docs.title: 🔔 Streaming Ticket Snapshots
docs.text:
Stream: snapshots of open position & pending-order tickets on a timer (OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData) — the lightweight way to watch what's open over time.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(interval_ms:) { |data| ... } (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets (defined in mt5-term-api-subscriptions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets(...) → stream
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::SubscriptionService::Stub#on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(request, metadata:, return_op:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A timer-driven stream of just the ticket ids of open positions and pending orders.
  • Why you need it. Detect opens/closes by diffing successive snapshots — no full order payloads.
  • Sanity check. Snapshots arrive ~once per interval_ms; the ticket sets match opened_orders_tickets.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: This is the push version of opened_orders_tickets: instead of polling, you get periodic ticket snapshots and compute the set difference to see exactly what opened or closed — cheap change-detection for a position monitor.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  def on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(interval_ms: 1000, &block) -> MetaRPC::MT5::Subscription
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description interval_ms Integer (keyword, default 1000) Snapshot interval. &block proc(data) Called per snapshot.

docs.title: ⬆️ Yielded
docs.text: Snapshot data carrying the current position tickets and pending-order tickets — diff successive snapshots to detect opens/closes cheaply.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Lightweight alternative to on_trade when you only track which tickets exist, not full detail.
  • Keep the previous snapshot to compute added = current - previous and removed = previous - current.
  • sub.cancel to stop.

docs.title: 1) Just wire it up
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(interval_ms: 1000) { |_d| }
sleep 5; sub.cancel

docs.title: 2) Detect opens / closes by diff
docs.text:
last = []
sub = acct.on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets do |d|
  cur = d.opened_position_tickets.to_a
  puts "opened: #{(cur - last).inspect}  closed: #{(last - cur).inspect}"
  last = cur
end

docs.title: 3) Faster polling
docs.text: acct.on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(interval_ms: 500) { |_d| }

docs.title: Fire a callback when a ticket closes
docs.text:
def on_close(acct, ticket, &cb)
  seen = false
  acct.on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets do |d|
    open = d.opened_position_tickets.to_a.include?(ticket)
    seen ||= open
    cb.call(ticket) if seen && !open
  end
end

docs.title: 🔔 Streaming Ticks
docs.text:
Stream: a tick for each price update on one or more symbols (MrpcSubscriptionMqlTick). Push, not poll.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#on_symbol_tick(symbols) { |tick| ... } (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Proto definition: OnSymbolTick (defined in mt5-term-api-subscriptions.proto)

docs.title: RPC
docs.text:
• Service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • Method: OnSymbolTick(OnSymbolTickRequest) → stream OnSymbolTickReply
  • Low-level client (generated): Mt5TermApi::SubscriptionService::Stub#on_symbol_tick(request, metadata:, return_op:)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A server stream that fires your block on every price change, on a background thread.
  • Why you need it. A live feed without polling — drive a dashboard, a trailing stop, or a signal.
  • Sanity check. sub.count climbs while an active symbol trades; sub.cancel stops it.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: on_symbol_tick is the real-time price source. Prefer it over polling symbol_info_tick in a loop: lower latency, less load, and it pushes only when something changes.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:
class MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Account
  # `symbols` is a String or Array. Returns a Subscription; call .cancel to stop.
  def on_symbol_tick(symbols, &block) -> MetaRPC::MT5::Subscription
end

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Parameter Type Description symbols String or [String] Symbol(s) to subscribe. &block proc(tick) Called per tick.

docs.title: ⬆️ Yielded — MrpcSubscriptionMqlTick
docs.text: Ruby accessor Type Description symbol String Which symbol. bid / ask / last Float Prices. volume / volume_real Integer / Float Tick volume. time / time_utc Timestamp Tick time (broker / UTC) — read .seconds. time_msc / time_msc_utc Integer Milliseconds. flags Integer Change flags bitmask.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Keep the block short — it runs on the reader thread; hand heavy work to a Queue.
  • Control handle: sub.cancel to stop, sub.count for ticks received, sub.error for a stored non-Cancelled error.
  • Blocking helper: for "collect for N seconds" use MT5Service#each_tick.

docs.title: 1) Live bid/ask for a basket
docs.text:
sub = acct.on_symbol_tick(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]) do |t|
  puts format("%-8s %s / %s", t.symbol, t.bid, t.ask)
end
sleep 5
sub.cancel

docs.title: 2) Count ticks over a window
docs.text:
n = 0
sub = acct.on_symbol_tick("EURUSD") { n += 1 }
sleep 3; sub.cancel
puts "#{n} ticks in 3s (sub.count=#{sub.count})"

docs.title: 3) Track the session high/low
docs.text:
hi, lo = -Float::INFINITY, Float::INFINITY
sub = acct.on_symbol_tick("EURUSD") { |t| hi = [hi, t.ask].max; lo = [lo, t.bid].min }
sleep 10; sub.cancel
puts "high #{hi}  low #{lo}"

docs.title: Hand ticks to a worker via a queue
docs.text:
q = Queue.new
sub = acct.on_symbol_tick("EURUSD") { |t| q << t }     # short: just enqueue
Thread.new { loop { tick = q.pop; heavy_process(tick) } }

docs.text:
• What it is. A server stream that fires on every order/position change — fills, modifications, closes.
  • Why you need it. React to executions the instant they happen instead of polling opened_orders.

docs.text: on_trade is the change notifier. Use it as the trigger to refresh your view of the book, log activity, or run follow-up logic — then read the authoritative state with opened_orders if you need full detail.

docs.title: 🔔 Streaming Trade Transactions
docs.text:
Stream: low-level MT5 trade-transaction events (OnTradeTransactionData) — the raw transaction feed behind every order lifecycle.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account#on_trade_transaction { |data| ... } (from the metarpc_mt5 gem)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The finest-grained trade feed — mirrors the MQL5 OnTradeTransaction event (request → order → deal).
  • Why you need it. Audit every step of an order's life, reconcile fills, or build precise execution analytics.
  • Sanity check. One order_send typically emits several transactions (more than on_trade).

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text: on_trade_transaction is the audit-grade stream. Where on_trade tells you "something changed", this tells you each underlying step — use it when you need the full execution trail rather than a summary.

docs.title: 🧱 Signature
docs.text:

docs.title: MT5Account · Streaming Methods — Overview
docs.text:
Real-time server streams: ticks, trade events, position-profit updates, ticket snapshots and raw trade transactions. Every stream runs on a background thread and hands you a Subscription.

All five live on mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService.

docs.title: 🔌 The stream contract
docs.text:
Each streaming method takes a block and returns a MetaRPC::MT5::Subscription:

sub = acct.on_symbol_tick("EURUSD") { |tick| puts "#{tick.bid}/#{tick.ask}" }
# ... later ...
sub.cancel          # stop the stream and join the reader thread
  • The SDK reads the stream on a background thread and calls your block per payload.
  • sub.cancel unsubscribes cleanly; sub.alive? tells you if it's still running; sub.count is how many messages arrived; sub.error holds a non-GRPC::Cancelled error if one occurred.
  • An error inside the stream is stored on sub.error (the thread doesn't crash your program).

docs.title: 📁 What lives here
docs.text: Method Yields OnSymbolTick a tick (MrpcSubscriptionMqlTick) per price update OnTrade OnTradeData when orders/positions change OnPositionProfit OnPositionProfitData on a timer OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets ticket snapshots on a timer OnTradeTransaction low-level OnTradeTransactionData events

docs.title: 🧭 Plain English
docs.text:
• Prices → on_symbol_tick. Any order/position change → on_trade. Live P/L → on_position_profit. Open tickets over time → on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets. Raw MT5 transactions → on_trade_transaction.

Rule of thumb: keep block handlers short (they run on the reader thread); hand heavy work to a queue.

docs.title: 🟢 Minimal snippet
docs.text:
n = 0
sub = acct.on_symbol_tick("EURUSD") { |t| n += 1 }
sleep 5
sub.cancel
puts "#{n} ticks in 5s"

docs.title: See also
docs.text:

  • Concepts: gRPC Stream Management.

docs.text:
Returned by account_info:

Field Type Description login Integer Account number. balance Float Balance (without floating P&L). equity Float Equity (balance + floating P&L). currency String Deposit currency. leverage Integer Leverage (100 = 1:100). trade_mode Symbol :MRPC_ACCOUNT_TRADE_MODE_DEMO / _CONTEST / _REAL. company String Broker name. server_time_utc Timestamp Broker server time in UTC (read .seconds).

docs.title: account_info -> Account
docs.text:
The account as one typed Struct.

Usage examples:

  1. One-line status: 
    a = service.account_info
puts "##{a.login} on #{a.company} · #{a.balance} #{a.currency} · 1:#{a.leverage}"
  2. Floating P&L (equity − balance): 
    a = service.account_info
puts "floating: #{(a.equity - a.balance).round(2)} #{a.currency}"
  3. Guard before a run: 
    a = service.account_info
abort "empty account" if a.balance <= 0

docs.title: account_summary -> AccountSummaryData
docs.text:
The full raw summary (every field, including all margin fields) when the Struct isn't enough.

Usage examples:

  1. Margin level: 
    puts service.account_summary.account_margin_level
  2. Full margin picture: 
    s = service.account_summary
puts "used #{s.account_margin}  free #{s.account_margin_free}  level #{s.account_margin_level}%"
  3. Terminal / trade flags: 
    s = service.account_summary
puts "trade allowed? #{s.account_trade_allowed}  EA allowed? #{s.account_trade_expert}"

docs.title: demo? -> Boolean
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Refuse to trade on a real account: 
    abort "refusing to trade on a REAL account" unless service.demo?
  2. Branch behaviour by mode: 
    volume = service.demo? ? 0.10 : 0.01
  3. Log the mode once at startup: 
    puts "mode: #{service.demo? ? 'DEMO' : 'LIVE'}"

docs.title: account_info_double(property) -> Float
docs.text:
One numeric property — pass an ACCOUNT_* symbol.

Usage examples:

  1. Free margin before sizing: 
    puts "free margin: #{service.account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE).round(2)}"
  2. Floating profit: 
    p = service.account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_PROFIT)
puts p.positive? ? "+#{p.round(2)}" : p.round(2)
  3. Margin-level gauge: 
    lvl = service.account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL)
puts lvl.zero? ? "flat" : (lvl < 200 ? "⚠️ low" : "✅ healthy")

docs.title: account_info_integer(property) -> Integer
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Leverage & login: 
    puts "##{service.account_info_integer(:ACCOUNT_LOGIN)} · 1:#{service.account_info_integer(:ACCOUNT_LEVERAGE)}"
  2. Is automated trading allowed? 
    puts service.account_info_integer(:ACCOUNT_TRADE_EXPERT) == 1 ? "EAs ok" : "EAs off"
  3. Margin mode: 
    puts ["netting", "exchange", "hedging"][service.account_info_integer(:ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE)]

docs.title: account_info_string(property) -> String
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Currency & company: 
    puts "#{service.account_info_string(:ACCOUNT_COMPANY)} — #{service.account_info_string(:ACCOUNT_CURRENCY)}"
  2. Trade server: 
    puts "server: #{service.account_info_string(:ACCOUNT_SERVER)}"
  3. Account holder: 
    puts "holder: #{service.account_info_string(:ACCOUNT_NAME)}"

The full property enums are listed on the low-level pages: AccountInfoDouble · Integer · String.

docs.title: quote(symbol) -> Quote
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Bid / ask / spread: 
    q = service.quote("EURUSD"); puts "#{q.bid}/#{q.ask} spread #{q.spread.round(5)}"
  2. Mid price: 
    q = service.quote("EURUSD"); puts ((q.bid + q.ask) / 2).round(5)
  3. Tick freshness: 
    q = service.quote("EURUSD"); puts "#{Time.now.utc.to_i - q.time_utc}s old"

docs.title: tick(symbol) -> MrpcMqlTick
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Raw tick volume: 
    puts service.tick("EURUSD").volume
  2. Spread in points: 
    t = service.tick("EURUSD"); pt = service.account.symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_POINT)
puts ((t.ask - t.bid) / pt).round
  3. Last deal price (0 on FX): 
    puts service.tick("XAUUSD").last

docs.title: symbols -> [String]
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Count & sample: 
    s = service.symbols; puts "#{s.size} symbols, first #{s.first}"
  2. Filter by prefix: 
    service.symbols.grep(/^EUR/).each { |s| puts s }
  3. Is a symbol listed? 
    puts service.symbols.include?("GBPUSD")

docs.title: symbols_total(market_watch_only:) -> Integer
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. All symbols: 
    puts service.symbols_total
  2. Market-Watch only: 
    puts service.symbols_total(market_watch_only: true)
  3. How many are hidden: 
    puts service.symbols_total - service.symbols_total(market_watch_only: true)

docs.title: symbol_name(index, selected:) -> String
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. First symbol: 
    puts service.symbol_name(0)
  2. First Market-Watch symbol: 
    puts service.symbol_name(0, selected: true)
  3. Walk a few: 
    (0...3).each { |i| puts service.symbol_name(i) }

docs.title: symbol_exist?(symbol) -> Boolean
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Guard a read: 
    abort "unknown symbol" unless service.symbol_exist?("EURUSD")
  2. Validate user input: 
    sym = "GBPUSD"; puts service.symbol_exist?(sym) ? "ok" : "no such symbol"
  3. Filter a list: 
    %w[EURUSD FOO BAR].select { |s| service.symbol_exist?(s) }

docs.title: symbol_synchronized?(symbol) -> Boolean
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. One-shot check: 
    puts service.symbol_synchronized?("EURUSD")
  2. Wait until synced: 
    sleep 0.2 until service.symbol_synchronized?("XAUUSD")
  3. Select then confirm: 
    service.select_symbol("GBPUSD"); puts service.symbol_synchronized?("GBPUSD")

docs.title: select_symbol(symbol, select = true) -> Boolean
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Show in Market Watch: 
    service.select_symbol("GBPUSD")
  2. Hide it again: 
    service.select_symbol("GBPUSD", false)
  3. Ensure before reading: 
    service.select_symbol("XAUUSD"); q = service.quote("XAUUSD")

docs.title: symbol_params(symbol) -> SymbolParameters | nil
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Lot limits: 
    sp = service.symbol_params("EURUSD"); puts "min #{sp.volume_min} step #{sp.volume_step}"
  2. Pip size: 
    sp = service.symbol_params("EURUSD")
puts sp.point * ([3, 5].include?(sp.digits) ? 10 : 1)
  3. Currencies: 
    sp = service.symbol_params("EURUSD"); puts "#{sp.currency_base}/#{sp.currency_profit}"

docs.title: symbol_params_all(sort:) -> [SymbolParameters]
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Count specs: 
    puts service.symbol_params_all.size
  2. Index by name (cache it): 
    specs = service.symbol_params_all.to_h { |s| [s.name, s] }
  3. Smallest min-lot symbols: 
    service.symbol_params_all.min_by(&:volume_min)

docs.title: margin_rate(symbol, type) -> SymbolInfoMarginRateData
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Initial / maintenance: 
    mr = service.margin_rate("EURUSD", :buy)
puts "#{mr.initial_margin_rate} / #{mr.maintenance_margin_rate}"
  2. Buy vs sell: 
    %i[buy sell].each { |t| puts "#{t}: #{service.margin_rate('EURUSD', t).initial_margin_rate}" }
  3. Pending type: 
    puts service.margin_rate("EURUSD", :buy_limit).initial_margin_rate

docs.title: tick_value_with_size(symbols) -> TickValueWithSizeData
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. One symbol (PascalCase accessors): 
    tv = service.tick_value_with_size("EURUSD").symbol_tick_size_infos.first
puts "value #{tv.TradeTickValue} size #{tv.TradeTickSize}"
  2. Several at once: 
    service.tick_value_with_size(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]).symbol_tick_size_infos.each { |x| puts "#{x.Name} #{x.TradeTickValue}" }
  3. Money per point: 
    tv = service.tick_value_with_size("EURUSD").symbol_tick_size_infos.first
pt = service.account.symbol_info_double("EURUSD", :SYMBOL_POINT)
puts (tv.TradeTickValue * (pt / tv.TradeTickSize)).round(4)

docs.title: session_quote(symbol, day_of_week:, session_index:) -> …
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Monday quote session: 
    sq = service.session_quote("EURUSD", day_of_week: :MONDAY)
puts "#{sq.from&.seconds}s → #{sq.to&.seconds}s"
  2. Whole week: 
    %i[MONDAY TUESDAY WEDNESDAY THURSDAY FRIDAY].each { |d| puts "#{d}: #{service.session_quote('EURUSD', day_of_week: d).from&.seconds}" }
  3. Second session of a day: 
    service.session_quote("XAUUSD", day_of_week: :MONDAY, session_index: 1)

docs.title: session_trade(symbol, day_of_week:, session_index:) -> …
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Monday trade session: 
    st = service.session_trade("EURUSD", day_of_week: :MONDAY)
puts "#{st.from&.seconds}s → #{st.to&.seconds}s"
  2. Compare quote vs trade window: 
    q = service.session_quote("EURUSD", day_of_week: :MONDAY)
t = service.session_trade("EURUSD", day_of_week: :MONDAY)
puts "quote #{q.from&.seconds} / trade #{t.from&.seconds}"
  3. Sunday (often closed): 
    service.session_trade("EURUSD", day_of_week: :SUNDAY)

docs.title: bars(symbol, timeframe:, …) -> [PriceBar]
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Last 5 H1 closes: 
    service.bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :H1, max_bars: 5).each { |b| puts b.close }
  2. Daily range of the last bar: 
    b = service.bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :D1, max_bars: 1).last
puts (b.high - b.low).round(5)
  3. A date window: 
    service.bars("EURUSD", timeframe: :M15, from_utc: Time.now.utc - 3600, to_utc: Time.now.utc)

docs.text:
Method Returns positions_total Integer opened_orders(sort:) OpenedOrdersData opened_tickets OpenedOrdersTicketsData positions(magic:, symbol:) [PositionInfo] (filtered) order_history(from_utc:, to_utc:, sort:, page_size:) [HistoryData] (auto-paged) positions_history(from_utc:, to_utc:, sort:, page_size:) [PositionHistoryInfo] (auto-paged)

docs.title: positions_total -> Integer
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Quick count: 
    puts "open: #{service.positions_total}"
  2. Gate new entries: 
    return if service.positions_total >= 5   # max 5 concurrent
  3. Flat check: 
    puts service.positions_total.zero? ? "flat" : "in market"

docs.title: opened_orders(sort:) -> OpenedOrdersData
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Positions vs pending: 
    d = service.opened_orders
puts "positions #{d.position_infos.size}  pending #{d.opened_orders.size}"
  2. Sorted newest first: 
    service.opened_orders(sort: :BMT5_OPENED_ORDER_SORT_BY_OPEN_TIME_DESC)
  3. Total floating P/L: 
    puts service.opened_orders.position_infos.sum(&:profit).round(2)

docs.title: opened_tickets -> OpenedOrdersTicketsData
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Count cheaply: 
    puts service.opened_tickets.opened_position_tickets.to_a.size
  2. Diff against a snapshot: 
    before = service.opened_tickets.opened_position_tickets.to_a
# ... later ...
after = service.opened_tickets.opened_position_tickets.to_a
puts "new: #{(after - before).inspect}"
  3. Pending order ids: 
    p service.opened_tickets.opened_orders_tickets.to_a

docs.title: positions(magic:, symbol:) -> [PositionInfo]
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. All open positions: 
    service.positions.each { |p| puts "##{p.ticket} #{p.symbol} P/L #{p.profit}" }
  2. One EA's positions: 
    service.positions(magic: 600_001).sum(&:profit)
  3. One symbol's positions: 
    service.positions(symbol: "EURUSD").size

docs.title: order_history(from_utc:, …) -> [HistoryData]
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Last 7 days of deals: 
    service.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7*24*3600).each do |h|
  d = h.history_deal; puts "deal ##{d.ticket} #{d.profit}" if d
end
  2. Realized P/L: 
    total = service.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30*24*3600)
               .filter_map { |h| h.history_deal&.profit }.sum
puts total.round(2)
  3. A specific window: 
    service.order_history(from_utc: Time.utc(2025, 1, 1), to_utc: Time.utc(2025, 2, 1))

docs.title: positions_history(from_utc:, …) -> [PositionHistoryInfo]
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Closed round-trips: 
    service.positions_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7*24*3600).each do |p|
  puts "##{p.position_ticket} #{p.symbol} #{p.profit}"   # note: position_ticket
end
  2. Win rate: 
    rows = service.positions_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30*24*3600)
puts "#{(100.0 * rows.count { |p| p.profit.positive? } / rows.size).round(1)}%"
  3. Best / worst trade: 
    rows = service.positions_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30*24*3600)
puts "best #{rows.max_by(&:profit)&.profit}  worst #{rows.min_by(&:profit)&.profit}"

Gotcha: PositionHistoryInfo exposes position_ticket (not ticket).

docs.title: MT5Service — Trading Methods (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
6 methods to place, modify and close orders, plus the pre-trade calculators — plain arguments, same exactly-once safety as the low layer.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a facade over MT5Account · Trading Operations.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt5/mt5_service.rb. Demos: examples/demos/service/04_service_demo.rb.

← MT5Service Overview

docs.title: ⚠️ Exactly-once trade safety
docs.text: order_send / order_modify / order_close are sent once and never re-sent. A transport failure after the request may have reached the terminal is raised as a TradeOutcomeUnknown-marked error — check positions/history before retrying. Trade retcode 10009 = DONE. See Return Codes.

docs.title: 📋 All 6 methods
docs.text:
Method Returns order_send(symbol:, type:, volume:, **opts) OrderSendData order_modify(ticket:, **opts) OrderModifyData order_close(ticket:, volume:, slippage:) OrderCloseData order_check(request) OrderCheckData order_calc_margin(symbol:, type:, volume:, price:) Float order_calc_profit(symbol:, type:, volume:, open_price:, close_price:) Float

type: — :buy / :sell / :buy_limit / :sell_limit / :buy_stop / :sell_stop / :buy_stop_limit / :sell_stop_limit.

docs.title: order_send(symbol:, type:, volume:, **opts) -> OrderSendData
docs.text:
Options: price:, stop_loss:, take_profit:, comment:, magic:, slippage:, stop_limit_price:, expiration_type:, expiration_utc:, without_checks:.

Usage examples:

  1. Market buy: 
    r = service.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, magic: 600_001)
puts r.returned_code == 10_009 ? "✅ ##{r.order}" : "❌ #{r.returned_code_description}"
  2. Market buy with SL/TP: 
    service.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, stop_loss: 1.08, take_profit: 1.09)
  3. Pending buy-limit below market: 
    bid = service.quote("EURUSD").bid
service.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy_limit, volume: 0.1, price: (bid - 0.003).round(5))

docs.title: order_modify(ticket:, **opts) -> OrderModifyData
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Set a stop-loss: 
    service.order_modify(ticket: 123_456, stop_loss: 1.085)
  2. Set both SL and TP: 
    service.order_modify(ticket: 123_456, stop_loss: 1.08, take_profit: 1.10)
  3. Move a pending order's price: 
    service.order_modify(ticket: 123_456, price: 1.0750)

docs.title: order_close(ticket:, volume:, slippage:) -> OrderCloseData
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Full close: 
    out = service.order_close(ticket: 123_456)
puts out.returned_code == 10_009 ? "closed" : out.returned_code_description
  2. Partial close (half): 
    service.order_close(ticket: 123_456, volume: 0.05)
  3. Delete a pending order: 
    service.order_close(ticket: pending_ticket)   # pending → deleted

docs.title: order_check(request) -> OrderCheckData
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Validate before sending: 
    req = Mt5TermApi::MrpcMqlTradeRequest.new(symbol: "EURUSD", volume: 0.1,
        order_type: :ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY, price: service.quote("EURUSD").ask)
service.order_check(req)
  2. Affordability gate: 
    res = service.order_check(req)
abort "would be rejected" unless res.mql_trade_check_result
  3. Reuse for several volumes: 
    [0.1, 1.0, 5.0].each do |v|
  r = Mt5TermApi::MrpcMqlTradeRequest.new(symbol: "EURUSD", volume: v, order_type: :ORDER_TYPE_TF_BUY, price: ask)
  puts "#{v}: #{service.order_check(r).mql_trade_check_result ? 'ok' : 'no'}"
end

docs.title: order_calc_margin(symbol:, type:, volume:, price:) -> Float
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Margin for 0.1 lot: 
    ask = service.quote("EURUSD").ask
puts service.order_calc_margin(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, price: ask).round(2)
  2. Fits free margin? 
    need = service.order_calc_margin(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 1.0, price: ask)
puts need <= service.account_info_double(:ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE) ? "ok" : "too big"
  3. Compare buy vs sell: 
    %i[buy sell].each { |t| puts "#{t}: #{service.order_calc_margin(symbol: 'EURUSD', type: t, volume: 0.1, price: ask).round(2)}" }

docs.title: order_calc_profit(symbol:, type:, volume:, open_price:, close_price:) -> Float
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. +100 points on 0.1 lot: 
    ask = service.quote("EURUSD").ask; pt = service.symbol_params("EURUSD").point
puts service.order_calc_profit(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, open_price: ask, close_price: ask + 100*pt).round(2)
  2. Short scenario: 
    service.order_calc_profit(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :sell, volume: 0.1, open_price: 1.10, close_price: 1.09)
  3. Risk/reward of an SL/TP: 
    risk   = service.order_calc_profit(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, open_price: 1.10, close_price: 1.095)
reward = service.order_calc_profit(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, open_price: 1.10, close_price: 1.115)
puts "R:R = #{(reward / -risk).round(2)}"
