docs.title: 📋 All 3 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Low-level equivalent book_add(symbol) Boolean market_book_add(symbol) book(symbol) MarketBookGetData market_book_get(symbol) book_release(symbol) Boolean market_book_release(symbol)

docs.title: book_add(symbol) -> Boolean
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Subscribe: 
    service.book_add("EURUSD")
  2. Guard before reading: 
    abort "no DOM" unless service.book_add("EURUSD")
  3. Subscribe several: 
    %w[EURUSD GBPUSD].each { |s| service.book_add(s) }

docs.title: book(symbol) -> MarketBookGetData
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Count levels: 
    puts service.book("EURUSD").mql_book_infos.size
  2. Top 5 levels: 
    service.book("EURUSD").mql_book_infos.first(5).each { |l| puts "#{l.type} #{l.price} x #{l.volume}" }
  3. Best bid / ask from the book: 
    levels = service.book("EURUSD").mql_book_infos
puts "levels: #{levels.size}" if levels.any?

docs.title: book_release(symbol) -> Boolean
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Release one: 
    service.book_release("EURUSD")
  2. Full add → read → release: 
    if service.book_add("EURUSD")
  puts service.book("EURUSD").mql_book_infos.size
  service.book_release("EURUSD")
end
  3. Release everything you added: 
    %w[EURUSD GBPUSD].each { |s| service.book_release(s) }

Always release what you add — leaving subscriptions open wastes gateway resources. Many FX symbols return an empty book.

docs.title: MT5Service — Streaming Methods (Mid-Level API)
docs.text:
6 methods for real-time streams. Each returns a Subscription running on a background thread — plus a blocking each_tick helper for scripts.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — a facade over MT5Account · Streaming.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt5/mt5_service.rb. Demos: examples/demos/service/05_service_streaming.rb.

← MT5Service Overview

docs.title: 🔌 The stream contract
docs.text:
Each streaming method takes a block and returns a MetaRPC::MT5::Subscription:

sub = service.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { |q| puts "#{q.bid}/#{q.ask}" }
sub.cancel        # stop & join the reader thread

sub.cancel stops cleanly; sub.alive? / sub.count / sub.error inspect it. Keep block handlers short — they run on the reader thread.

docs.title: subscribe_ticks(symbols) { |tick| … } -> Subscription
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. One symbol: 
    sub = service.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { |t| puts "#{t.bid}/#{t.ask}" }
sleep 5; sub.cancel
  2. Several symbols: 
    service.subscribe_ticks(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]) { |t| puts "#{t.symbol} #{t.bid}" }
  3. Count ticks: 
    n = 0; sub = service.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { n += 1 }
sleep 3; sub.cancel; puts "#{n} ticks"

docs.title: each_tick(symbols, seconds:) { |tick| … } -> Integer
docs.text:
The blocking convenience: subscribe, iterate for seconds, auto-cancel, return the count.

Usage examples:

  1. Collect for 4 s: 
    puts service.each_tick("EURUSD", seconds: 4) { |t| puts t.bid }
  2. Track the high: 
    hi = 0.0; service.each_tick("EURUSD", seconds: 5) { |t| hi = [hi, t.ask].max }
puts "high #{hi}"
  3. Multiple symbols: 
    service.each_tick(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD], seconds: 3) { |t| puts t.symbol }

docs.title: on_trade { |event| … } -> Subscription
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Log events: 
    sub = service.on_trade { |ev| puts "event #{ev.type}" }
sleep 10; sub.cancel
  2. Re-read the book on a change: 
    service.on_trade { |_ev| puts service.positions_total }
  3. Count events in a window: 
    n = 0; sub = service.on_trade { n += 1 }; sleep 5; sub.cancel; puts n

docs.title: on_position_profit(interval_ms:, ignore_empty:) { |data| … } -> Subscription
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Floating P/L every second: 
    service.on_position_profit(interval_ms: 1000) { |d| puts d.updated_positions.sum(&:profit).round(2) }
  2. Alert on drawdown: 
    service.on_position_profit { |d| puts "⚠️" if d.updated_positions.sum(&:profit) < -50 }
  3. Count updated positions: 
    sub = service.on_position_profit { |d| puts d.updated_positions.size }; sleep 5; sub.cancel

docs.title: on_tickets(interval_ms:) { |data| … } -> Subscription
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Watch ticket sets: 
    sub = service.on_tickets(interval_ms: 1000) { |_d| }; sleep 5; sub.cancel
  2. Detect new opens cheaply (diff snapshots): 
    last = []
service.on_tickets { |d| cur = d.opened_position_tickets.to_a; puts (cur - last).inspect; last = cur }

    service.on_tickets(interval_ms: 500) { |_d| }

docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Raw transaction feed: 
    sub = service.on_trade_transaction { |txn| puts txn.inspect[0, 80] }
sleep 10; sub.cancel

    n = 0; sub = service.on_trade_transaction { n += 1 }; sleep 5; sub.cancel; puts n
  3. Error-safe reader: 
    sub = service.on_trade_transaction { |_t| }
sleep 5; sub.cancel; warn sub.error if sub.error

docs.title: MT5Service — Mid-Level API Overview
docs.text:
A convenient wrapper over MT5Account that returns plain Ruby objects (Structs) and plain arguments instead of protobuf messages.

🧩 API Layer: MID-LEVEL — the balance between low-level (MT5Account) and high-level (MT5Sugar).

docs.title: ⚠️ Same calls, cleaner results
docs.text:
MT5Service and MT5Account make the same gRPC calls — the difference is the return shape, not the logic.

# Low-level (MT5Account) — you read the protobuf tick:
t = account.symbol_info_tick("EURUSD")
spread = t.ask - t.bid

# Mid-level (MT5Service) — you get a tidy Quote struct:
q = service.quote("EURUSD")       # Quote(symbol, bid, ask, last, spread, time_utc)
spread = q.spread

What the mid layer does for you

  • ✅ Builds the protobuf *Request from plain arguments.
  • ✅ Returns typed Ruby Structs where they add value — Account, Quote.
  • ✅ Auto-pages history reads and hands back ready arrays.
  • ✅ Filters positions in Ruby (positions(magic:, symbol:)).
  • ✅ Keeps the raw protobuf *Data where the full shape matters (orders, specs, order book) — one hop from the low layer.

Both layers are equally valid — pick the altitude you prefer. For one-liners, go up again to MT5Sugar.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture layers
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  MT5Sugar      one-liners, risk-based sizing│  ← highest
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  MT5Service    plain args → typed structs   │  ← YOU ARE HERE
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  MT5Account    raw protobuf / gRPC          │  ← lowest
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Each layer owns the one below it: MT5Sugar owns an MT5Service, which owns an MT5Account. From here you can always drop down with service.account.

docs.title: 🧱 Construction & lifecycle
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt5"

# Build a fresh MT5Account underneath, or wrap one you already have:
service = MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Service.new(api_key: ENV["MRPC_API_KEY"])
# service = MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Service.new(existing_account)

service.connect(5057947437, "password", server: "MetaQuotes-Demo")

a = service.account_info            # Account struct
puts "#{a.login}  #{a.balance} #{a.currency}  1:#{a.leverage}"

service.disconnect
  • MT5Service.new(account = nil, **opts) → wraps account, or builds a fresh MT5Account from **opts (api_key:, id:, host, port, timeout:).
  • service.account → the underlying MT5Account (drop down a layer any time).
  • service.connect(login, password, server:) — also connect_by_host / connect_proxy.
  • service.disconnect(delete:) — pass delete: true to free the terminal (otherwise it stays warm).

Tuning timeouts. Unary reads use the underlying account.timeout (seconds, default 60); set service.account.timeout = 30 to change it.

docs.title: 🧾 The typed objects (Structs)
docs.text:
MT5Service returns two Structs; everything else is the raw protobuf *Data (one hop from MT5Account).

Struct From Fields Account account_info login, balance, equity, currency, leverage, trade_mode, company, server_time_utc Quote quote symbol, bid, ask, last, spread, time_utc

Raw protobuf still comes back from: positions / opened_orders (PositionInfo), order_send (OrderSendData), symbol_params (SymbolParameters), bars (PriceBar[]), book (MarketBookGetData), history methods (HistoryData / PositionHistoryInfo).

docs.title: 1) Account snapshot
docs.text:
a = service.account_info
puts "##{a.login} · #{a.balance} #{a.currency} · 1:#{a.leverage}"

docs.title: 2) Current price
docs.text:
q = service.quote("EURUSD")
puts "Bid #{q.bid}, Ask #{q.ask}, Spread #{q.spread.round(5)}"

docs.title: 3) Validate → place an order
docs.text:
r = service.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.1, stop_loss: 1.08, take_profit: 1.09)
puts r.returned_code == 10_009 ? "✅ order ##{r.order}" : "❌ #{r.returned_code_description}"

docs.title: 4) Live price + floating P&L
docs.text:
t = service.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { |q| puts "tick #{q.bid} #{q.ask}" }
p = service.on_position_profit { |d| puts "floating: #{d.updated_positions.sum(&:profit).round(2)}" }
# later: t.cancel; p.cancel

docs.title: 📊 Low-level vs mid-level
docs.text: Aspect MT5Account (low) MT5Service (mid) Arguments plain args, builds *Request plain args Return protobuf *Data Struct (where it helps) or *Data Quotes symbol_info_tick → tick quote → Quote(bid, ask, spread, …) Account account_summary → *Data account_info → Account struct History manual paging auto-paged arrays Best for every field, full control everyday app code

docs.title: 🔧 Best practices
docs.text:
1. Handle errors with begin/rescue. Every method raises on failure — a server rejection raises MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError (carrying the mql / trade codes), a transport failure raises the gRPC error.
begin
  a = service.account_info
rescue MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError => e
  warn "failed: #{e.message}"
end

  1. Check the trade retcode. order_send / order_modify / order_close return a result with a returned_code — 10009 = DONE. A transport failure after the request may have reached the terminal is raised as a TradeOutcomeUnknown-marked error — do not blindly retry.

  2. Tune the timeout via service.account.timeout (seconds) for slow links or heavy history pulls.

  3. Always cancel streaming subscriptions when done — they run on a background thread and don't stop on their own.

  4. Free the terminal with service.disconnect(delete: true) at the end of a one-shot run (a trial allows one terminal per IP).

docs.text: MT5Service is the everyday layer: the same gRPC calls as MT5Account, but plain arguments in and tidy Ruby objects out — typed Account / Quote Structs, auto-paged history, filtered positions, no manual request building. Drop to MT5Account for full control, go up to MT5Sugar for one-liners.

docs.title: connect(login, password, server:, **opts) -> ConnectData
docs.text:
ConnectEx by broker server name. Raises InvalidLoginError on bad credentials (never retry that).

Usage examples:

  1. Basic connect: 
    mt5.connect(5057947437, "password", server: "MetaQuotes-Demo")
  2. Name the terminal + longer login wait: 
    mt5.connect(5057947437, "password", server: "MetaQuotes-Demo", name: "bot", timeout_seconds: 180)
  3. Handle a bad login: 
    begin
  mt5.connect(1, "wrong", server: "MetaQuotes-Demo")
rescue MetaRPC::MT5::InvalidLoginError => e
  warn "bad login: #{e.message}"
end

docs.text:
Connect by the broker's raw trade-server host:port (no cluster lookup).

Usage examples:

    mt5.connect_by_host(5057947437, "password", host: "mt5.broker.com", port: 443)
  2. With a name: 
    mt5.connect_by_host(5057947437, "password", host: "mt5.broker.com", port: 443, name: "bot")
  3. Fallback after a cluster-name miss: 
    mt5.connect(5057947437, "password", server: "Broker-Live") rescue
  mt5.connect_by_host(5057947437, "password", host: "mt5.broker.com", port: 443)

docs.text:
Positional-server shorthand for connect.

    mt5.quick_connect(5057947437, "password", "MetaQuotes-Demo"); puts mt5.balance

6 helpers for real-time streams. Each returns a Subscription (background thread) — plus a blocking each_tick.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — wraps MT5Service / MT5Account streams.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt5/mt5_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/* · lowlevel/03_streaming_methods.rb.

← MT5Sugar Overview

docs.title: 🔌 The stream contract
docs.text:
Each streaming method takes a block and returns a MetaRPC::MT5::Subscription:

sub = mt5.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { |t| puts "#{t.bid}/#{t.ask}" }
sub.cancel          # stop & join the reader thread

sub.cancel stops cleanly; sub.count / sub.error inspect it. Keep handlers short — they run on the reader thread.

docs.title: 📋 All 6 methods
docs.text: Method Yields subscribe_ticks(symbols) a tick per update on_trade OnTradeData on_position_profit(interval_ms:, ignore_empty:) OnPositionProfitData on_tickets(interval_ms:) ticket snapshots on_trade_transaction OnTradeTransactionData each_tick(symbols, seconds:) (blocking) → Integer

docs.title: subscribe_ticks(symbols) { |tick| … }
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. One symbol: 
    sub = mt5.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { |t| puts "#{t.bid}/#{t.ask}" }; sleep 5; sub.cancel
  2. Basket: 
    mt5.subscribe_ticks(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD]) { |t| puts "#{t.symbol} #{t.bid}" }
  3. Count: 
    n = 0; sub = mt5.subscribe_ticks("EURUSD") { n += 1 }; sleep 3; sub.cancel; puts n

docs.title: each_tick(symbols, seconds:) { |tick| … } -> Integer
docs.text:
Blocking: subscribe, iterate for seconds, auto-cancel, return the count.

Usage examples:

  1. Collect for 4 s: 
    puts mt5.each_tick("EURUSD", seconds: 4) { |t| puts t.bid }
  2. Track the high: 
    hi = 0.0; mt5.each_tick("EURUSD", seconds: 5) { |t| hi = [hi, t.ask].max }; puts hi
  3. Several symbols: 
    mt5.each_tick(%w[EURUSD GBPUSD], seconds: 3) { |t| puts t.symbol }

docs.title: on_trade · on_position_profit · on_tickets · on_trade_transaction
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Trade events: 
    sub = mt5.on_trade { |ev| puts ev.type }; sleep 10; sub.cancel
  2. Live floating P/L: 
    mt5.on_position_profit(interval_ms: 1000) { |d| puts d.updated_positions.sum(&:profit).round(2) }
  3. Ticket diffs / raw transactions: 
    mt5.on_tickets { |d| p d.opened_position_tickets.to_a }
mt5.on_trade_transaction { |txn| puts txn.inspect[0, 60] }

docs.text:
6 one-liners for the money numbers — each reads one account property as a plain Float.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — wraps MT5Account#account_info_double.

← MT5Sugar Overview

docs.title: 📋 All 6 methods
docs.text: Method Returns Property balance Float :ACCOUNT_BALANCE equity Float :ACCOUNT_EQUITY margin Float :ACCOUNT_MARGIN free_margin Float :ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE margin_level Float :ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL (percent) profit Float :ACCOUNT_PROFIT (floating)

docs.title: balance -> Float
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Print it: 
    puts mt5.balance.round(2)
  2. Empty-account guard: 
    abort "no funds" if mt5.balance <= 0
  3. Risk budget (1% of balance): 
    risk = mt5.balance * 0.01

docs.title: equity -> Float
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Print it: 
    puts mt5.equity.round(2)
  2. Floating P&L: 
    puts (mt5.equity - mt5.balance).round(2)
  3. Equity-stop trigger: 
    mt5.close_all_positions if mt5.equity < mt5.balance * 0.9

docs.title: margin -> Float
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Used margin: 
    puts mt5.margin.round(2)
  2. Margin utilisation: 
    puts "#{(100 * mt5.margin / mt5.equity).round(1)}% used"
  3. Is anything open (by margin)? 
    puts mt5.margin.zero? ? "flat" : "in market"

docs.title: free_margin -> Float
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Available margin: 
    puts mt5.free_margin.round(2)
  2. Can I afford this trade? 
    need = mt5.required_margin("EURUSD", 0.1, mt5.ask("EURUSD"))
puts mt5.free_margin >= need ? "ok" : "too big"
  3. Max lot shorthand: 
    puts mt5.max_lot("EURUSD", mt5.ask("EURUSD"))

docs.title: margin_level -> Float
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Percent: 
    puts "#{mt5.margin_level.round(1)}%"
  2. Health gauge: 
    lvl = mt5.margin_level
puts lvl.zero? ? "flat" : (lvl < 200 ? "⚠️ low" : "✅ healthy")
  3. Margin-call watch: 
    warn "near margin call!" if mt5.margin_level.positive? && mt5.margin_level < 120

docs.title: profit -> Float
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Floating profit: 
    puts mt5.profit.round(2)
  2. In profit? 
    puts mt5.profit.positive? ? "green" : "red"
  3. Take-profit on the whole book: 
    mt5.close_all_positions if mt5.profit >= 100

docs.title: bid(symbol) -> Float
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Print it: 
    puts mt5.bid("EURUSD")
  2. Place a stop below bid: 
    sl = mt5.bid("EURUSD") - 0.0020
  3. Poll a basket: 
    %w[EURUSD GBPUSD].each { |s| puts "#{s} #{mt5.bid(s)}" }

docs.title: ask(symbol) -> Float
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Print it: 
    puts mt5.ask("EURUSD")
  2. Margin at the ask: 
    puts mt5.required_margin("EURUSD", 0.1, mt5.ask("EURUSD")).round(2)
  3. Mid price: 
    puts ((mt5.bid("EURUSD") + mt5.ask("EURUSD")) / 2).round(5)

docs.title: spread(symbol) -> Float
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Price-unit spread: 
    puts mt5.spread("EURUSD").round(5)
  2. Spread in points: 
    puts (mt5.spread("EURUSD") / mt5.symbol_point("EURUSD")).round
  3. Skip wide spreads: 
    return if mt5.spread("EURUSD") / mt5.symbol_point("EURUSD") > 30

docs.title: price(symbol) -> Quote
docs.text:

  1. One snapshot, all fields: 
    q = mt5.price("EURUSD")
puts "#{q.bid}/#{q.ask} spread #{q.spread.round(5)}"
  2. Tick age: 
    q = mt5.price("EURUSD"); puts "#{Time.now.utc.to_i - q.time_utc}s old"
  3. Pre-trade snapshot: 
    q = mt5.price("EURUSD"); mt5.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.01) if q.spread < 0.0002

docs.text:
One-liners to open market and pending orders. Each returns OrderSendData — check returned_code (10009 = DONE).

docs.title: ⚠️ Results, not exceptions
docs.text: A broker rejection comes back as returned_code (not an exception). Only a hard failure raises (ApiError / TradeOutcomeUnknown). Always check the retcode.

docs.title: 📋 All methods
docs.text:
Method Order buy_market(symbol, volume, **kw) (alias buy) market buy sell_market(symbol, volume, **kw) (alias sell) market sell buy_limit(symbol, volume, price, **kw) pending buy limit sell_limit(symbol, volume, price, **kw) pending sell limit buy_stop(symbol, volume, price, **kw) pending buy stop sell_stop(symbol, volume, price, **kw) pending sell stop

**kw: magic:, comment:, stop_loss:, take_profit:, slippage:, …

docs.title: buy_market(symbol, volume, **kw) (alias buy)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Simple buy: 
    r = mt5.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.01)
puts r.returned_code == 10_009 ? "##{r.order}" : r.returned_code_description
  2. Tag with magic & comment: 
    mt5.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.01, magic: 600_001, comment: "entry")
  3. Alias form: 
    mt5.buy("EURUSD", 0.01)

docs.title: sell_market(symbol, volume, **kw) (alias sell)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Simple sell: 
    mt5.sell_market("EURUSD", 0.01)
  2. With slippage: 
    mt5.sell_market("EURUSD", 0.01, slippage: 30)
  3. Alias form: 
    mt5.sell("EURUSD", 0.01)

docs.title: buy_limit(symbol, volume, price, **kw)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Below the market: 
    mt5.buy_limit("EURUSD", 0.01, (mt5.bid("EURUSD") - 0.0030).round(5))
  2. With SL/TP: 
    px = (mt5.bid("EURUSD") - 0.0030).round(5)
mt5.buy_limit("EURUSD", 0.01, px, stop_loss: px - 0.005, take_profit: px + 0.010)
  3. Tagged: 
    mt5.buy_limit("EURUSD", 0.01, 1.0750, magic: 42)

docs.title: sell_limit(symbol, volume, price, **kw)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Above the market: 
    mt5.sell_limit("EURUSD", 0.01, (mt5.ask("EURUSD") + 0.0030).round(5))
  2. Tagged: 
    mt5.sell_limit("EURUSD", 0.01, 1.1050, comment: "fade")
  3. Check the retcode: 
    r = mt5.sell_limit("EURUSD", 0.01, 1.1050); puts r.returned_code

docs.title: buy_stop(symbol, volume, price, **kw)
docs.text:
Breakout above the market.

    mt5.buy_stop("EURUSD", 0.01, (mt5.ask("EURUSD") + 0.0030).round(5))
  2. With a stop-loss:

mt5.buy_stop("EURUSD", 0.01, px, stop_loss: px - 0.004)
  3. Tagged: 
    mt5.buy_stop("EURUSD", 0.01, 1.1050, magic: 7)

mt5.sell_stop("EURUSD", 0.01, px, stop_loss: px + 0.004)

docs.text:
Open a market position with protection attached, and adjust stops on an open position.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — wraps MT5Account#order_send / #order_modify.

docs.title: 📋 All 5 methods
docs.text: Method Does buy_market_with_sl_tp(symbol, volume, sl:, tp:, **kw) market buy + SL/TP sell_market_with_sl_tp(symbol, volume, sl:, tp:, **kw) market sell + SL/TP modify_sl(ticket, stop_loss) set/move the stop-loss modify_tp(ticket, take_profit) set/move the take-profit modify_sl_tp(ticket, stop_loss:, take_profit:) set both at once

docs.title: buy_market_with_sl_tp(symbol, volume, sl:, tp:, **kw)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Fixed prices: 
    mt5.buy_market_with_sl_tp("EURUSD", 0.01, sl: 1.0800, tp: 1.1000)
  2. Pip-based around the market: 
    pip = mt5.symbol_point("EURUSD") * 10
q = mt5.price("EURUSD")
mt5.buy_market_with_sl_tp("EURUSD", 0.01, sl: (q.bid - 20*pip).round(5), tp: (q.ask + 40*pip).round(5))
  3. Tagged: 
    mt5.buy_market_with_sl_tp("EURUSD", 0.01, sl: 1.08, tp: 1.10, magic: 600_001)

docs.title: sell_market_with_sl_tp(symbol, volume, sl:, tp:, **kw)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Fixed prices: 
    mt5.sell_market_with_sl_tp("EURUSD", 0.01, sl: 1.1050, tp: 1.0900)
  2. 2:1 reward/risk: 
    q = mt5.price("EURUSD")
mt5.sell_market_with_sl_tp("EURUSD", 0.01, sl: (q.ask + 0.0020).round(5), tp: (q.bid - 0.0040).round(5))
  3. Check the retcode: 
    r = mt5.sell_market_with_sl_tp("EURUSD", 0.01, sl: 1.1050, tp: 1.0900); puts r.returned_code

docs.title: modify_sl(ticket, stop_loss)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Set a stop-loss: 
    mt5.modify_sl(123_456, 1.0850)
  2. Move to break-even: 
    pos = mt5.position(123_456); mt5.modify_sl(pos.ticket, pos.price_open) if pos
  3. Trail behind bid: 
    mt5.modify_sl(123_456, (mt5.bid("EURUSD") - 0.0015).round(5))

docs.title: modify_tp(ticket, take_profit)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Set a take-profit: 
    mt5.modify_tp(123_456, 1.1000)
  2. Extend the target: 
    mt5.modify_tp(123_456, (mt5.ask("EURUSD") + 0.0050).round(5))
  3. Remove it (0 = none): 
    mt5.modify_tp(123_456, 0.0)

docs.title: modify_sl_tp(ticket, stop_loss:, take_profit:)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Both at once: 
    mt5.modify_sl_tp(123_456, stop_loss: 1.0850, take_profit: 1.1000)
  2. From the entry price: 
    p = mt5.position(123_456)
mt5.modify_sl_tp(p.ticket, stop_loss: p.price_open - 0.005, take_profit: p.price_open + 0.010) if p
  3. Tighten on profit: 
    mt5.modify_sl_tp(123_456, stop_loss: (mt5.bid("EURUSD") - 0.0010).round(5), take_profit: 1.1050)

docs.title: 📋 All 6 methods
docs.text: Method Does close_position(ticket, volume:, slippage:) close one (full or partial) close_all_positions(slippage:) close every open position close_all_by_symbol(symbol, slippage:) close all positions on a symbol order_send(symbol:, type:, volume:, **opts) raw order (any type/options) order_modify(ticket:, **opts) raw modify order_close(ticket:, **opts) raw close / delete pending

docs.title: close_position(ticket, volume: nil, slippage: 10)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Full close: 
    out = mt5.close_position(123_456)
puts out.returned_code == 10_009 ? "closed" : out.returned_code_description
  2. Partial close: 
    mt5.close_position(123_456, volume: 0.05)
  3. Close the newest on a symbol: 
    pos = mt5.open_positions(symbol: "EURUSD").max_by(&:ticket)
mt5.close_position(pos.ticket) if pos

docs.title: close_all_positions(slippage: 10)
docs.text:
Closes every open position; returns an array of results.

Usage examples:

  1. Flatten everything: 
    mt5.close_all_positions
  2. Count how many closed: 
    puts "closed #{mt5.close_all_positions.size}"
  3. Panic button on drawdown: 
    mt5.close_all_positions if mt5.profit < -100

docs.title: close_all_by_symbol(symbol, slippage: 10)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Flatten one symbol: 
    mt5.close_all_by_symbol("EURUSD")
  2. Results: 
    puts mt5.close_all_by_symbol("EURUSD").map(&:returned_code).inspect
  3. Rotate out of a symbol: 
    mt5.close_all_by_symbol("GBPUSD"); mt5.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.01)

docs.title: order_send(symbol:, type:, volume:, **opts)
docs.text:
Raw passthrough — full control when a helper is too narrow (drop-in with the old flat client).

Usage examples:

  1. Any order type: 
    mt5.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy_stop_limit, volume: 0.01, price: 1.1050, stop_limit_price: 1.1045)
  2. Without checks: 
    mt5.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy, volume: 0.01, without_checks: true)
  3. With expiry: 
    mt5.order_send(symbol: "EURUSD", type: :buy_limit, volume: 0.01, price: 1.0750, expiration_utc: Time.now.utc + 3600)

docs.title: order_modify(ticket:, **opts) · order_close(ticket:, **opts)
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Raw modify: 
    mt5.order_modify(ticket: 123_456, stop_loss: 1.0850)
  2. Raw close:

  3. Delete a pending order:

docs.title: MT5Sugar — History & Statistics (High-Level API)
docs.text:
2 helpers for closed history — orders+deals, and round-trips. Both auto-page and take a UTC start.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — wraps MT5Service#order_history / positions_history.

Implementation: lib/metarpc_mt5/mt5_sugar.rb. Demos: examples/demos/sugar/09_sugar_history.rb.

← MT5Sugar Overview

docs.title: 📋 All 2 methods
docs.text:
Method Returns order_history(from_utc:, **opts) [HistoryData] (orders + deals) positions_history(from_utc:, **opts) [PositionHistoryInfo] (round-trips)

**opts: to_utc: (default now), sort:, page_size:.

docs.title: order_history(from_utc:, **opts) -> [HistoryData]
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Last 7 days of deals: 
    mt5.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7*24*3600).each do |h|
  d = h.history_deal; puts "deal ##{d.ticket} #{d.profit}" if d
end
  2. Realized P&L: 
    total = mt5.order_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30*24*3600)
           .filter_map { |h| h.history_deal&.profit }.sum
puts total.round(2)
  3. A calendar window: 
    mt5.order_history(from_utc: Time.utc(2025,1,1), to_utc: Time.utc(2025,2,1))

docs.title: positions_history(from_utc:, **opts) -> [PositionHistoryInfo]
docs.text:
Usage examples:

  1. Closed round-trips: 
    mt5.positions_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 7*24*3600).each do |p|
  puts "##{p.position_ticket} #{p.symbol} #{p.profit}"   # note: position_ticket
end
  2. Win rate: 
    rows = mt5.positions_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30*24*3600)
puts "#{(100.0 * rows.count { |p| p.profit.positive? } / rows.size).round(1)}%"
  3. Best / worst: 
    rows = mt5.positions_history(from_utc: Time.now.utc - 30*24*3600)
puts "best #{rows.max_by(&:profit)&.profit}  worst #{rows.min_by(&:profit)&.profit}"

docs.title: MT5Sugar — High-Level API Overview
docs.text:
One-line helpers for everyday trading: connect, read balances, quote, buy/sell, manage positions, size risk, stream. The friendliest layer — built on MT5Service, which is built on MT5Account.

🧩 API Layer: HIGH-LEVEL — maximum convenience, minimum boilerplate.

docs.title: 🧱 One call builds the whole stack
docs.text:
require "metarpc_mt5"

mt5 = MetaRPC::MT5::MT5Sugar.create("mt5.mrpc.pro", 443, api_key: ENV["MRPC_API_KEY"])
mt5.connect(5057947437, "password", server: "MetaQuotes-Demo")

r = mt5.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.10)
mt5.modify_sl_tp(r.order, stop_loss: 1.0850, take_profit: 1.1000)
puts "balance #{mt5.balance.round(2)}"
  • MT5Sugar.create(host = "mt5.mrpc.pro", port = 443, **opts) → builds MT5Sugar → MT5Service → MT5Account (opts: api_key:, id:, timeout:).
  • mt5.service → the mid layer · mt5.account → the low layer. Drop down any time.
  • MetaRPC::MT5::Client aliases MT5Sugar — a drop-in friendly entry point.

docs.title: 🛑 How errors surface
docs.text:
Trading one-liners (buy_market, close_position, …) return the result *Data — check returned_code (10009 = DONE):

r = mt5.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.10)
puts r.returned_code == 10_009 ? "✅ ##{r.order}" : "❌ #{r.returned_code_description}"

A hard failure still raises: a server-side error raises MetaRPC::MT5::ApiError, and a transport failure after the request may have reached the terminal raises a TradeOutcomeUnknown-marked error — don't blindly retry a trade. Read helpers (balance, bid, connected?) return plain values.

docs.title: 🧮 Pips on MT5
docs.text: Pip size = point × (digits == 3 || digits == 5 ? 10 : 1). So on 5-digit EURUSD one pip = 0.0001, on 3-digit JPY pairs one pip = 0.01. Read point / digits with symbol_point / symbol_digits.

docs.title: Strategies — Master Overview
docs.text: Orchestrators and presets built on MT5Sugar — small, readable strategy demos you can run and adapt.

docs.title: ⚠️ Educational demos only
docs.text: Every orchestrator and preset here is a demonstration template, not a production trading system. They use simple signals, no real risk engine, and fixed parameters. Run them on a demo account. Before anything live: understand the algorithm, backtest, forward-test, and add real risk management.

docs.title: 🧩 What's an orchestrator vs a preset?
docs.text:
• Orchestrator — composes several MT5Sugar one-liners into one full strategy lifecycle (open → manage → close). It runs a single playbook.
  • Preset — the layer above orchestrators: it reads the market and picks which orchestrator fits right now. The "brain" / router.
Preset  ─ reads conditions ─▶  picks an Orchestrator  ─ composes ─▶  MT5Sugar one-liners

docs.title: 📁 Orchestrators
docs.text: # Strategy Idea Trades? 11 Trailing Stop open, then ratchet the stop-loss up behind price, lock in profit ⚠ yes (demo) 13 Grid Trader bracket the market with pending limits + stops, then remove them ⚠ yes (demo) 14 Risk Manager monitor floating drawdown, flatten everything on breach (kill-switch) dry-run by default

docs.title: 📁 Presets

docs.title: ▶️ Running them
docs.text:
All are registered demos — launch from the interactive menu or directly:

ruby examples/demos/main.rb         # menu
ruby examples/demos/main.rb 11      # trailing stop
ruby examples/demos/main.rb 16      # adaptive preset (read-only)

Credentials come from examples/demos/config/config.json or the MT5_* env vars (see Getting Started).

docs.title: 🪜 Grid Trader Orchestrator
docs.text:
Bracket the market with a symmetric grid of pending orders, list them, then remove them. ⚠ Places real (demo) pending orders, then cancels them.

Demo: examples/demos/orchestrators/13_grid_trader.rb · Run: ruby examples/demos/main.rb 13

docs.title: 💡 What it is
docs.text: A grid surrounds the current price with pending orders so you're positioned whichever way the market breaks. This demo shows the mechanics — it places the grid and then removes it (no position management), so you can see how limits and stops bracket the market.

docs.title: 🧠 Strategy logic
docs.text:
At each level i (spaced step_pts apart from the market) it places four pending orders:

Order Where Fires when… buy_limit below the market price dips into it (join the pullback) sell_limit above the market price rallies into it (fade the spike) buy_stop above the market price breaks out up sell_stop below the market price breaks down

Limits face the market (mean-reversion); stops break out with momentum. Whichever zone price enters, an order triggers.

docs.title: 🧱 Composed from (MT5Sugar)
docs.text: Step Methods Place price · buy_limit/sell_limit/buy_stop/sell_stop List sugar.account.opened_orders.opened_orders (raw layer) Remove order_close(ticket:) (deletes a pending)

docs.title: 🔧 Code walkthrough
docs.text:
levels = 2         # per side
step_pts = 300     # spacing, points
q = sugar.price(sym)

placed = []
(1..levels).each do |i|
  buy_price  = (q.bid - i * step_pts * point).round(digits)   # below
  sell_price = (q.ask + i * step_pts * point).round(digits)   # above
  b  = sugar.buy_limit(sym,  vol, buy_price)
  s  = sugar.sell_limit(sym, vol, sell_price)
  bs = sugar.buy_stop(sym,   vol, sell_price)   # breakout up
  ss = sugar.sell_stop(sym,  vol, buy_price)    # breakout down
  placed.push(b.order, s.order, bs.order, ss.order)
end

# remove the grid — order_close on a pending ticket deletes it
placed.each { |t| sugar.order_close(ticket: t) rescue nil }

docs.title: ⚙️ Tunables
docs.text:
Name Meaning levels number of price levels per side step_pts spacing between levels, in points (wider = fewer, farther orders)

Make it real: keep the grid live, watch fills via on_trade, and add take-profit / stop-loss and a close_all_by_symbol exit.

docs.title: ⚠️ Safety
docs.text: Places 4 × levels pending orders and deletes them. Demo accounts only. A level may trigger before removal — the demo guards each order_close with rescue.

docs.title: 🛡️ Risk Manager Orchestrator
docs.text:
Monitor the account and flatten everything if floating drawdown breaches a limit — a kill-switch you run alongside a trading strategy. Safe by default (dry-run).

Demo: examples/demos/orchestrators/14_risk_manager.rb · Run: ruby examples/demos/main.rb 14

docs.title: 💡 What it is
docs.text: The other orchestrators open trades; this one protects them. It polls the account and, once unrealized losses get too big, closes every position to cap the damage. In practice it runs in parallel with whatever strategy is trading.

docs.title: 🧠 Strategy logic
docs.text:
Floating drawdown is unrealized loss as a fraction of balance:

floating = equity − balance
drawdown = max(0, −floating) / balance

On each check it recomputes drawdown; once it crosses max_drawdown, the kill-switch fires → close_all_positions. With dry_run = true (the default) it only reports what would happen, so the demo never closes anything.

docs.title: 🧱 Composed from (MT5Sugar)
docs.text: Step Methods Monitor balance · equity · count_positions Enforce close_all_positions

docs.title: 🔧 Code walkthrough
docs.text:
dry_run = true          # true = report only
max_drawdown = 0.50     # fire at 50% of balance lost (floating)

checks.times do
  sleep 1
  balance  = sugar.balance
  equity   = sugar.equity
  floating = equity - balance
  dd = balance.zero? ? 0.0 : (floating.negative? ? -floating / balance : 0.0)

  if dd >= max_drawdown
    sugar.close_all_positions unless dry_run   # kill-switch
    break
  end
end

docs.title: ⚙️ Tunables
docs.text:
Name Meaning dry_run true = report only · false = actually flatten max_drawdown drawdown fraction that fires the switch (e.g. 0.10 = 10%) checks how many times the demo polls

Make it real: replace the fixed checks loop with an on_position_profit stream so the switch reacts live, and run it as a separate supervisor thread next to your strategy.

docs.title: ⚠️ Safety
docs.text: Read-only by default (dry_run = true) — it never closes anything until you arm it. When armed, close_all_positions is irreversible. Demo accounts only.

docs.title: 🎯 Trailing Stop Orchestrator
docs.text:
Open a position, then ratchet its stop-loss up behind the price to lock in profit as the market moves your way. ⚠ Places a real (demo) order.

Demo: examples/demos/orchestrators/11_trailing_stop.rb · Run: ruby examples/demos/main.rb 11

docs.title: 💡 What it is
docs.text: A trailing stop is the simplest profit-protection strategy: you enter, and every tick you move the stop-loss to a fixed distance behind the current price — but only upward. If price keeps rising, the stop follows and your locked-in profit grows; if price pulls back into the stop, you're taken out with the gains you'd already secured.

docs.title: 🧠 Strategy logic
docs.text:
On each tick the orchestrator computes a candidate stop:

candidate_sl = bid − trail_pts × point

and applies the ratchet rule — move the stop there only if it's higher than the best stop so far:

if candidate_sl > best_sl    → modify_sl(ticket, candidate_sl)   # tighten
else                          → hold (never loosen)

That one-way ratchet is the whole idea: the stop can only improve, never give back ground.

docs.title: 🧱 Composed from (MT5Sugar)
docs.text: Step Methods Open buy_market · open_positions Trail bid · modify_sl · symbol_point · symbol_digits Close close_position

docs.title: 🔧 Code walkthrough
docs.text:
point  = sugar.symbol_point(sym)
digits = sugar.symbol_digits(sym)
trail_pts = 150      # stop sits this far below bid
steps = 6            # how many ticks to trail for

# 1. OPEN — buy, then grab the position's ticket
res = sugar.buy_market(sym, vol, magic: 110_011)
pos = sugar.open_positions(symbol: sym).max_by(&:ticket)

# 2. TRAIL — ratchet the stop up, never down
best_sl = nil
steps.times do
  sleep 1
  bid  = sugar.bid(sym)
  want = (bid - trail_pts * point).round(digits)
  if best_sl.nil? || want > best_sl
    best_sl = want
    sugar.modify_sl(pos.ticket, want)          # tighten only
  end
end

# 3. CLOSE — exit (a real run lets the stop do it)
sugar.close_position(pos.ticket)

docs.title: ⚙️ Tunables
docs.text:
Name Meaning trail_pts trail distance in points (smaller = tighter, gets stopped sooner) steps how many ticks the demo trails for

Make it real: replace the fixed steps loop with a subscribe_ticks stream and let the broker's stop close the position (drop the explicit close_position).

docs.title: ⚠️ Safety
docs.text: Places one tiny market position and closes it. Demo accounts only. Respect the symbol's min_stop_level — a stop too close to price is rejected.

docs.title: 🧭 Adaptive Market Mode Preset
docs.text:
Measure the market (spread + recent volatility) and recommend which orchestrator to run. Fully read-only — it decides, it doesn't trade.

Demo: examples/demos/presets/16_adaptive_preset.rb · Run: ruby examples/demos/main.rb 16

docs.title: 💡 What it is
docs.text:
An orchestrator runs one strategy. A preset is the layer above: it reads conditions and routes to the orchestrator that fits right now. This one is the "brain" that chooses between Trailing Stop, Grid Trader, and Risk Manager.

measure spread + volatility  ─▶  pick a playbook  ─▶  (a real preset launches it)

docs.title: 🧠 Decision logic
docs.text:
Two signals drive the choice:

  • spread (in points) — how costly/illiquid the market is right now.
  • ATR proxy — the average H1 high-low range over the last 24 bars (a volatility estimate).
Condition Pick Why spread > 50 pts [14] Risk Manager costly/illiquid — don't enter actively, just watch risk ATR > 400 pts [11] Trailing Stop strong directional moves — ride them, protect profit otherwise (calm) [13] Grid Trader range-bound chop — harvest the range with a grid

docs.title: 🧱 Composed from (MT5Sugar)
docs.text: Step Methods Signals spread · bars · symbol_point Decide pure Ruby — map signals to a recommendation

docs.title: 🔧 Code walkthrough
docs.text:
point = sugar.symbol_point(sym)

# 1. SIGNALS
spread_pts = (sugar.spread(sym) / point).round
bars = sugar.bars(sym, timeframe: :H1, max_bars: 24)
ranges  = bars.map { |b| (b.high - b.low) / point }
atr_pts = ranges.empty? ? 0 : (ranges.sum / ranges.size).round

# 2. DECIDE
pick =
  if    spread_pts > 50 then "14 Risk manager"
  elsif atr_pts    > 400 then "11 Trailing stop"
  else                       "13 Grid trader"
  end
puts "→ run demo [#{pick}]"

docs.title: ⚙️ Tunables
docs.text:
Name Meaning spread threshold (50) above this, the market is treated as too costly to enter ATR threshold (400) above this, the market is treated as "trending/volatile" H1 lookback (24) how many bars feed the volatility estimate

Make it real: instead of printing the pick, launch the chosen orchestrator (call its block), and re-evaluate on a schedule so the bot adapts as conditions change.

docs.title: ⚠️ Safety
docs.text: Fully read-only — it only analyses and prints a recommendation. Nothing is traded.
